scores.quote: The revision of transaction charges for BSE Derivatives segment significantly contributed our financial performance this quarter.

scores.rationale: The company is at a cyclical high, not near a bottom — 13 consecutive record-revenue quarters, record IPO year, record SIP flows and peak retail participation leave the identifiable move ahead as downward rather than upward.
scores.quote: BSE delivered its 13th consecutive quarter of record revenues

scores.rationale: The end market is in genuine secular expansion — investor accounts from 11 crore (2022) to 25 crore (2026), SIP flows to Rs.3.5 lakh crore and DII deployment of Rs.8.5 lakh crore absorbing FPI outflows — reflecting durable financialisation of Indian household savings.
scores.quote: SIP flows reached a record Rs. 3.5 lakh crores for the year

scores.rationale: Organic focus with no large M&A, a debt-free balance sheet, and a self-imposed, threshold-capped SGF contribution policy that was proactively dialled down once the buffer was met, demonstrates prudent, rules-based stewardship.
scores.quote: we are reducing the contribution requirement per quarter from 5% to 3.5%

scores.rationale: The CEO's multi-year derivatives revival (expiry-day changes, relaunch, single-stock derivatives, Thursday cycle) was pursued through repeated regulatory and SGF headwinds across FY24-FY25 and delivered by FY26.
scores.quote: BSE in the last 18 months has faced multiple headwinds and it has emerged stronger

scores.rationale: Management communication is process- and market-development oriented and explicitly disclaims profit-chasing, though the scripted political tributes to the PM and FM in later calls dilute the substance-over-showmanship impression.
scores.quote: we don't strive hard to protect the top line or bottom line

scores.rationale: Little systematic talent-development disclosure across sixteen calls; a dedicated Chief of Staff and HR Strategy role appears only in FY26, and the leadership roster shows repeated turnover in CFO, CIO, CBO and CTO seats rather than a visible internal pipeline.
scores.quote: Dr. Vivek Jain - Chief of Staff and HR Strategy

scores.rationale: Management gives specific, unflattering detail when pressed — admitting StAR MF realisation decline, MTM treasury losses and an ECL provision on an Rs.80cr NSE receivable — but routinely declines granularity on pricing slabs and forward realisations.
scores.quote: There is an outstanding of Rs. 80 crore, which is an old outstanding from NSE

scores.rationale: A large share of the earnings explosion traces to exogenous factors — SEBI's true-to-label pricing mandate, expiry-day calendar reshuffles and regulatory constraints on the competitor — so the record results overstate demonstrable management skill and the assessment is not robust to halo.
scores.quote: The Bankex contracts have also generated significant interest since its expiry date changed to Monday from October 16, 2023

scores.rationale: BSE holds monopoly-like positions in specific niches — the SME platform (60% share, 700 listings) and the Sensex brand in the retail mind — but is the clear number two in the main cash and derivatives franchises.
scores.quote: BSE's SME platform achieved a significant milestone with the successful listing of its 700th SME company

scores.rationale: StAR MF is deeply integrated with AMCs and distributors and described as systemically critical, creating real switching costs, and index licensing to 350+ clients with Rs.2.7 lakh crore of benchmarked passive AUM is similarly sticky.
scores.quote: systemically critical distribution channel within India's mutual fund landscape

scores.rationale: Indian exchanges are a regulated duopoly rather than a broad oligopoly — brokers and retail end-customers have negligible negotiating power over charges — but duopoly with one dominant player is a weaker structure than a stable multi-player oligopoly, and BSE's clearing arm even services its rival.
scores.quote: our group's clearing company, ICCL, provides services to both BSE and NSE

scores.rationale: SEBI licensing makes entry effectively impossible and ownership is stable, but pricing rationality has been imperfect — BSE deliberately underpriced option contracts versus the incumbent to buy share, as analysts noted in FY26.
scores.quote: Your option contracts are still quite lower than competition

scores.rationale: The share BSE has taken has come from a strong, well-capitalised NSE rather than weak donators; only in peripheral segments (legacy MF distribution channels, contingency power markets) are there genuinely weak incumbents to feed on.
scores.quote: we have observed a pronounced expansion in open interest, deeper market participation

scores.rationale: BSE is the opposite of under-the-radar — a 150-year-old listed icon covered by IIFL, Motilal Oswal, Jefferies and 360 One on these very calls, with heavy retail and media attention on every regulatory development.
scores.quote: the celebration of BSE's 150th anniversary

scores.rationale: The Sensex name carries genuine brand equity that converted into a globally traded options franchise at very high gross margin, though pricing power is capped by SEBI's charge framework and by competitive undercutting rather than being freely exercised.
scores.quote: Sensex index options has consequently advanced to rank among the most actively traded contracts in 2025

scores.rationale: Exchange and clearing customers buy certainty above all, and BSE consistently sells that — glitch-free operation, a Rs.1,202cr core SGF buffer, and a re-engineered real-time risk system — with reliability, not price, the stated basis for large participants joining ICCL.
scores.quote: BSE's core SGF balance stood at Rs. 1,202 crores

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a real and improving edge — colocation for latency-sensitive clients, 25 crore investor accounts, and the India Post tie-up extending mutual-fund access into rural and semi-urban India — though direct customer intimacy runs through brokers rather than BSE itself.
scores.quote: BSE signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Department of Posts (DoP)

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — reliability and TCO plus integration lock-in for corporate customers (brokers, AMCs, 350+ index clients, issuers) alongside the intangible Sensex brand for the retail end — even if BSE's revenue depends on intermediaries it does not control.
scores.quote: serving over 350 marquee clients both domestically and globally

scores.rationale: Technology capability has improved dramatically (trades per second per broker scaled roughly ninefold, peak 69,000) and is now an enabler of member acquisition, but this is catch-up parity with the incumbent rather than a deep, multi-product technological edge.
scores.quote: handle around 29,000 trades per second per broker

scores.rationale: StAR MF is a genuine two-sided AMC-distributor network that strengthens with scale, and Sensex options have shown liquidity begetting liquidity, but in the core cash market BSE remains on the losing side of a rival's stronger network effect.
scores.quote: Following the transition to a Thursday expiry cycle, we have seen broadening of the liquidity profile

scores.rationale: StAR MF is India's largest mutual fund distribution platform at 84 crore annual transactions and an 8.2 crore monthly peak, and the exclusive first-mover Department of Posts integration extends reach into rural India that rivals cannot readily replicate.
scores.quote: This partnership leverages the vast postal network to democratize investment across India.

scores.rationale: Investment is in people/capabilities rather than hard capex, and the returns have been poor — FY26 revenue fell 6% in dollar terms despite years of 'sustained investments'.
scores.quote: we will continue to make investments that are necessary to build a differentiated value proposition in the marketplace

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or brand-promotion spend in any of the excerpts.
Platform investment (Cogito, AI orchestration layers) has produced some marquee AI wins, but there is no disclosed R&D intensity or evidence of durable payback since revenue is shrinking.
scores.quote: we are deploying our AI -powered solution s, including our Cogito platform

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed anywhere in the excerpts.
Consistent dividend policy (interim plus final, INR 6.50 for FY26) funded by strong cash generation, though there is no buyback or explicit valuation-linked framework.
scores.quote: takes our overall dividend for the full financial year to INR 6.50 per share

scores.rationale: Asset-light services model with best-in-class DSO and a large net-cash balance sheet, but no protecting moat — revenue is declining and pricing is being conceded.
scores.quote: our DSO has improved quarter -on-quarter and now stands at 54 days, which yo u would agree is amongst the best in our industry

scores.rationale: As a ~$600m player it has ample runway, but it is losing rather than gaining share — FY26 revenue degrew 6% in dollar terms while peers grew.
scores.quote: our revenues were down 1.2% in rup ee terms to INR 53,100 million

scores.rationale: Rest-of-World grew strongly and sales capacity is being added in US and Europe with a San Francisco alliances leader, but geographies remain small and there is no premium brand that travels.
scores.quote: our Rest of the World business has also registered a strong growth in Q1

scores.rationale: Growth is not price-led at all — AI deals require upfront productivity give-backs and the offshore/fixed-price shift lowers realisation even as volumes rise.
scores.quote: upfront productivity benefits that we ha d to pass on because of AI deals that we have won

scores.rationale: Demand has been depressed for many quarters and management believes the trough is passed, but the same 'green shoots' claim has been made repeatedly since FY25 without a turn.
scores.quote: we are hoping that the bad ne ws is behind us now and FY'27 will be better for us

scores.rationale: Enterprise digital/AI adoption is secular, but for Birlasoft AI is currently revenue-deflationary and its ERP and manufacturing end-markets are contracting.
scores.quote: our ERP business has been very challenged

scores.rationale: Purely organic strategy with no M&A, a debt-free balance sheet with INR 2,637 crore cash, and continued investment through the downturn.
scores.quote: We ended the year with cash and cash equivalents of INR 2,637.3 crore, up 19% year -on-year

scores.rationale: Long-term intent is clearly articulated and investment continues through weakness, but the record is of unmet ambitions — the FY23 'billion-dollar strategy' never materialised and FY26 revenue is lower.
scores.quote: We are not here for one quarter or two. We are here to the build business for a decade.

scores.rationale: Calls are plain, numbers-led and management makes no personality-driven claims; the CEO consistently defers detail to the CFO and functional leaders.
Leadership is being rebuilt almost entirely through external Tier-1 hires (COO, ERP, Data/AI, Life Sciences, Americas) after senior exits, indicating a weak internal pipeline.
scores.quote: These leaders that we have added have all com e in from Tier 1 companies

scores.rationale: The current CEO openly owns underperformance including multi-year failures, a marked improvement on the FY23 management that denied any execution problem while missing targets.
scores.quote: We've consistently not performed on our ERP business.

scores.rationale: The headline story is 333bps of margin expansion, but management itself attributes a large part to forex, one-offs and exiting revenue — skill is hard to separate from accounting tailwinds while the top line shrinks.
scores.quote: gains from ex change rate tailwind s, about 70 to 80 basis points, as well as from one -offs, about 110 basis points

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in any niche — even its historic ERP/JDE stronghold has been losing revenue for multiple years.
scores.quote: we will see softness in the ERP business for another quarter at least

scores.rationale: Switching costs are evidently weak: projects are deferred, cancelled or lost on client-specific decisions and staff-aug work is being competed away.
scores.quote: an operational issue at one of our customers affected our volume growth

scores.rationale: Mid-tier Indian IT is fragmented and customers hold clear negotiating power, dictating discretionary cuts and productivity pass-throughs.
scores.quote: customers have been holding back on discretionary spend and are pushing for productivity benefits

scores.rationale: Low entry barriers and irrational economics are evident — the company had to exit whole revenue streams that were unprofitable and concede price to win AI work.
scores.quote: bold decisions that we took of walking away from several non -profitable revenue streams

scores.rationale: On the evidence Birlasoft is the donor rather than the taker, ceding revenue in ERP, manufacturing and life sciences over successive years.
scores.quote: That reflects the challenging demand environment... some headwinds because of that in account -specific issues

scores.rationale: It is a mid-cap in a heavily analysed sector — the calls feature Nomura, Macquarie, Kotak and Emkay — so it is niche in size but not ignored by capital.
scores.quote: The next question is from the line of Ravi Menon from Macquarie.

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; demand is unsteady and the customer conversation is about cost optimisation, not brand.
scores.quote: Customers continue to focus on optimizing their spends , and discretionary spending therefore remains constrained.

scores.rationale: Some deals are won on domain credibility rather than price, but reliability has not prevented project deferrals or account-specific revenue erosion.
scores.quote: Many of these deals were won on the back of our domain expertise and AI -led capabilities.

scores.rationale: Sales reach is admittedly sub-scale — management is raising seller headcount 30-40% precisely because coverage has been inadequate.
scores.quote: our sales team strength would have gone up by 30 % to 40% on a year -on-year basis

scores.rationale: Purely corporate/enterprise customers with strong procurement leverage and no lock-in, extracting productivity give-backs rather than paying for TCO certainty.
scores.quote: our clients are also challenging us to do more outcome -based work

scores.rationale: There is a proprietary AI/agentic platform winning flagship engagements, but it is a services wrapper on partner stacks (SAP, Google, AWS) rather than a deep multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: a multi -year engagement to design, build, and deploy AI agents across a customer's business ecosystem

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the excerpts.
Distribution is a weakness, not a moat — the FY26 diagnosis of the revenue decline centres on insufficient sales capacity and pipeline generation.
scores.quote: Our focus going forwar d will only be centered around sales, pipeline generation , and order booking

scores.rationale: Genuine growth capex into backward-integrated upper/sneaker manufacturing (Paonta Sahib stabilized, Pantnagar commissioned Jan 2026, targeting 8-9 lakh sneaker pairs/month), but incremental returns are unproven as ROCE has fallen from 37.4% in Q1FY23 to 22.4% in FY26.
scores.quote: the capacity for Pantnagar for example after 2 phases of development can go up to 6 lakh pairs of sneakers per month... we are targeting in totality 8-9 lakh pair monthly production

scores.rationale: A&P is treated as long-term brand investment (~10-11% of sales, protected even in downturns) and the 'You Go, Girl' campaign demonstrably lifted the women's mix from 18.7% to 22%, though spend has risen much faster than the ~11% revenue growth it supports.
scores.quote: we have taken a fairly aggressive budget in FY27 on the marketing side... we don't want to deliver margins just by cutting corners with respect to marketing

scores.rationale: No formal R&D, but design/NPD is systematic and productive — ~250 new SKUs in FY26, 78 new designs in a single quarter, and an 80-100 day time-to-market that produced a sneaker portfolio doubling year on year.
scores.quote: Our accelerated time to market of 80-100 days enabled by a fully integrated manufacturing ecosystem gives us a distinct edge

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed in any excerpt; the only 'acquisition' referenced is a 71-year land lease for the Pantnagar plant, which is capex rather than M&A.
scores.quote: The Pantnagar facility which we acquired, technically it is on a 71-year lease from the state government

scores.rationale: Buybacks, dividends or any distribution policy are never mentioned across the excerpts.

Returns remain respectable (ROCE 22.4%, ROE 18.1% in FY26) but the model is deliberately becoming more asset-heavy through in-house plants and ROCE has compressed from 37.4% in FY23, with no hard moat protecting the turn.
scores.quote: return on capital employed has also gone up from 29.7% in FY22 to 37.4% in TTM Q1FY23

scores.rationale: Campus is a mid-sized player with runway in a fragmented category and claims share gains backed by distribution expansion to 29,000+ touchpoints and 18-19% online growth, but the FY24-25 de-growth phase shows gains have not been continuous.
scores.quote: we should grow you know in line or faster than the category. So, I don't see any challenge with respect to our market share increase

scores.rationale: Expansion is purely intra-India (South/West EBOs, state-specific distribution strategies) with exports only an aspiration under new FTAs — no executed international footprint for a brand that has not yet been shown to travel.
scores.quote: with free trade agreements being signed... would you be like exploring this opportunity going forward? ... Yes, absolutely. It is an exciting

scores.rationale: FY26 revenue growth of 11.4% was led by a 7% ASP rise driven by premium sneakers (~INR 910 ASP) and richer women's/kids mix, with volumes contributing only low single digits.
scores.quote: The average selling price grew by 7% year-on-year from INR 658 to INR 683... premiumization trend remains firmly in our favor

scores.rationale: The company passed through a clear demand trough in FY24-FY25 (heatwave, channel destocking, B2B collapse) and is now on the upswing with festive demand and GST rationalisation as identifiable tailwinds.
scores.quote: The robust demand during the festive season coupled with the positive impact of GST rationalization has further accelerated our performance

scores.rationale: Sports/athleisure footwear is described as the fastest-growing footwear category in India for six consecutive years, driven by casualisation and low penetration — a genuinely secular end market.
scores.quote: The whole sports athleisure space is growing faster than any other footwear category currently for the last, I think five years, 6 consecutive years now

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic with no M&A, low leverage (net debt/EBITDA 0.4x), disciplined working capital and an explicit choice to prioritise profitability over store expansion, though the earlier over-reliance on B2B e-commerce channels showed lapses.
scores.quote: While we prioritize profitability over aggressive retail expansion this year, our exclusive brand outlet network remains steady at 300 stores

scores.rationale: Multi-year initiatives — the 18-24 month pivot from outright to marketplace online, backward integration into uppers/sneakers, and apparel entry — were pursued through a weak demand cycle and are now visibly converting into growth.
scores.quote: We have done a lot of interventions over the past 3 years to bring a sustainable growth and predictable growth to the organization... a lot of those initiatives... are now materializing

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly declines to give forward guidance and keeps commentary operational rather than promotional, with celebrity association confined to the brand (Kriti Sanon) rather than the executives.
scores.quote: on the forward-looking, I don't think we will be able to give any specifics on the guidance

scores.rationale: Headcount is being added in front-end and stores and a CBO/COO layer has been built out, but senior roles (CFO change in FY24, externally hired CBO) show no evidence of a systematic internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: this is primarily driven by our additional headcounts primarily in the front-end function, the distribution business and also in the stores

scores.rationale: Management quantifies awkward items (Rs 10 cr e-com accounting change, Rs 65.4 cr lease distortion), openly explains the FY25 inventory correction and B2B base effect, and acknowledges investor apprehension about volatility rather than deflecting it.
scores.quote: Gaurav, we understand your apprehensions. That is what we are trying to fix.

scores.rationale: The spectacular FY23 optics (150% YoY growth, 37% ROCE) were a COVID-rebound artefact that reversed into de-growth and near-halved ROCE, so results should be separated from skill — the recent recovery is credible but not yet proof of durable execution.
scores.quote: Revenue from operations increased by 149.6% year on year to INR 338 crores during the quarter

scores.rationale: Campus holds no monopoly-like position in the consumer's mind — it competes across price points against MNCs and domestic brands and positions itself on value ('premium sneakers at affordable prices') rather than uniqueness.
scores.quote: As pioneers in offering Premium Sneakers at affordable prices, we remain committed to making high-quality design-forward footwear accessible

scores.rationale: Consumer footwear carries no switching costs, no captive aftermarket and no regional exclusivity — the customer can substitute brands freely at every purchase.
The Indian footwear market is highly fragmented across organised brands, unorganised players and imports, and powerful e-commerce platforms hold negotiating leverage over commissions.
scores.quote: Online commission again is a dynamic negotiation between our platforms or the channel partners

scores.rationale: BIS quality certification has raised a real regulatory barrier and curtailed cheap imports, but the category still has low intrinsic entry barriers and heavy marketplace-driven price competition.
scores.quote: BIS is fully in effect now as of 1st of August... the Chinese inventory and the fake things that are being imported from China has reduced significantly

scores.rationale: Non-BIS unorganised players and Chinese import channels are being forced out of the market, and management points to weakening competition as a source of the northern-region mix gain.
scores.quote: the government has mandated time till end of June 2025 for everyone to liquidate their non-BIS inventory... The imports have also been largely curtailed

scores.rationale: This is a widely covered listed consumer name with CLSA, Kotak, JM, Ambit, Motilal Oswal and others on every call — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: the line of Aditya Soman from CLSA

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 53.5% and successful premiumisation plus a full-range April price hike show real brand-based pricing power, though the company earlier absorbed wage inflation rather than pass it on and admits price resistance risk.
scores.quote: we chose not to pass on these higher cost to our consumers during these subdued market conditions

scores.rationale: There is a mild trust/quality angle (BIS compliance, 'trusted brand for the entire family') but footwear buyers here are clearly price- and fashion-sensitive rather than paying for certainty.
scores.quote: reinforcing Campus as a trusted brand for the entire family

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a core strength — 23,100 retailers growing to 29,000 touchpoints, 300 EBOs, super-stockist restructuring and direct marketplace/brand.com presence give broad and deepening customer reach.
scores.quote: Campus Activewear product range has further enhanced to 650 plus new retail outlets, raising the total count to 23,100 plus retailers across the country

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely retail and the benefit set offered — brand campaigns, design refresh, premiumisation and accessibility — is correctly matched to intangible-driven consumer demand.
scores.quote: the campaign resonated strongly with our female consumers, resulting in an improvement in the women's category mix

scores.rationale: There is no meaningful technology edge or R&D intensity; the advantage claimed is design speed and in-house assembly, which is an operational capability replicable by scaled rivals.
scores.quote: With more than 90% of our raw materials sourced locally and all assembly conducted in-house

scores.rationale: A single-sided consumer footwear brand has no self-reinforcing network; scale brings distribution leverage, not network effects, and nothing in the calls suggests otherwise.

Pan-India reach across ~29,000 touchpoints, 300 EBOs, a new super-stockist tier and state-specific distribution strategies is the company's strongest asset and the main driver of recent growth, though larger domestic rivals match or exceed this reach.

scores.rationale: Reach is real — service infrastructure, data centres, processing capacity and specialised sales teams across segments — but the advantage is described more as product/platform superiority than an unmatchable service network.

scores.rationale: Across all four transcripts management discusses balance-sheet growth, provisions and capital, but never branch/technology capital expenditure or incremental ROIC on growth investment.

No R&D disclosure; the only product-innovation reference is a retail gold-loan variant, with no spend or efficiency data.

scores.quote: we are continuing to improve our market share every year -on-year . This is the very one few banks , one am ong the few banks that their market share in the housing is increasing

scores.quote: in our bank we don't buy any portfolio buy out and we hardly participate in the co -lending portfolio

scores.rationale: Four different MD&CEOs across the 17 calls (Prabhakar, Satyanarayana Raju, Ahluwalia, Brajesh Kumar Singh), with government-appointed leaders arriving from other PSU banks — structurally limiting independent, long-horizon stewardship.
scores.quote: I have got experience of Indian Bank also... at the same time, I am having experience of 28 years at Bank of Baroda also

scores.rationale: Calls are uniformly low-key, numbers-first and free of personality promotion, with the MD deferring to vertical heads and EDs for detail.

scores.rationale: Some internal progression (Satyanarayana Raju and Ahluwalia both moved ED to MD&CEO) and a Rs 300 crore performance-linked incentive provision, but the top job is ultimately filled by external government appointment rather than an internal pipeline.

scores.rationale: Management volunteers unflattering detail and reconciles it clearly — the profit drop was attributed to one-off listing gains and MTM losses, the yield decline to a penal-interest reclassification, and the low CASA/NIM position is openly conceded.

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented and the bank is a price-taker on the liability side — forced to pay up for deposits amid competition from peers and mutual funds — so end customers hold the negotiating power.

scores.rationale: Licensing limits new entrants, but pricing is visibly irrational: the bank had to walk away from 22,500 crore of underpriced corporate loans and repeatedly raise deposit rates to defend share.

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power: NIM of ~2.52% is peer-worst, CASA is below 30%, and the bank competes by paying higher deposit rates rather than charging a brand premium.

scores.quote: now almost 85% plus of our customers are at a quarterly reset

scores.rationale: Commentary is uniformly operational and metric-driven with no promotional framing or personality-building across all 17 calls.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across any of the three calls.

scores.rationale: The parent-bank bancassurance counter functions as a quasi-captive channel with real distribution lock-in, but it is already open architecture and the DFS is signalling further opening, so the protection is partial at best.

scores.rationale: Indian life insurance is fragmented rather than oligopolistic — the company ranks 9th among private players and the FDI limit rising to 100% is expected to invite further participation.

scores.rationale: Regulatory capital and solvency requirements are real barriers and management calls distributor payouts 'rationalized', but 100% FDI plus pending regulation on agency commissions point to more capital and competition entering, not less.
scores.quote: we are also seeing that the distributor payouts are also kind of forgetting kind of rationalized to some extent

scores.rationale: Clear evidence of weaker players donating share — the company grew 19-20% in FY26 against 10% industry growth, took rank from a peer, and describes LIC's share on the Canara counter as minuscule.

scores.rationale: The core proposition is certainty and it is being delivered and measured — claim settlement ratio 99.4%→99.6%, NPS 76→80, and persistency improving across every cohort and line of business.

scores.rationale: Distribution intimacy is the central advantage — embedded in Canara Bank and HSBC branches with analytics identifying high-propensity customers, giving accessibility a standalone insurer cannot replicate.
scores.quote: increased branch activation and strategic efforts to penetrate deeper into Tier-3 and tier 4 markets, driven through customer segmentation and data analytics into high-propensity customers

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to customer segment — HSBC's higher-risk-appetite affluent base gets ULIP (60%), a distinct annuity-seeking cohort is targeted analytically, and captive bank borrowers take credit life growing 40-50%.

scores.rationale: Digital, GenAI and analytics investment is real and a Chief Strategy and Data Officer is in place, but it is efficiency tooling rather than a deep, differentiating multi-product technology edge.

scores.rationale: Nothing in any call speaks to a two-sided or self-reinforcing network.

scores.quote: broadly, 70% of the business comes from Canara. And another 14% to 15% comes from HSBC

scores.rationale: Sustained platform investment of ~20% of revenue on technology teams plus capitalised migration/AI tooling is growth- not maintenance-oriented and shows up as rising cash returns, though reported ROCE is still only 3%.

scores.rationale: Spend is enterprise sales-led rather than brand advertising, but it is disciplined and productive — 17% of topline on sales described as best-in-class while new ACV held at INR121 crores and US logos scaled.

scores.rationale: R&D consistently converts into new products and customers — aiRA went from free pilots in Feb 2026 to a few million dollars of revenue with ~25% of customers piloting or paying by May 2026, alongside the top Forrester Wave rating.

scores.rationale: Repeatable, cheaply priced roll-up (0.5–1.5x revenue, 4-year cash payback, 30%→65% gross margin post-migration) with contractual protection actually enforced, but the acquirees are weak/declining assets and SessionM at $35m is no longer a small bolt-on.
scores.quote: let's go buy some of these competitors at 0.5x to 1.5x revenue and migrate those customers over ourselves

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed in either call; the company is freshly listed and holding INR463 crores of cash for M&A.

Asset-light subscription model with 69-70% gross margins, upfront billing and 22% cash ROIC protected by integration switching costs, but reported ROCE of just 3% reflects the acquisition-heavy balance sheet.
scores.quote: a more relevant term for a cash -generating business like ours is a cash return on invested c apital, and this stands at 22%

scores.rationale: Small absolute share in a fragmented 30-40 year old industry with demonstrated capture — new order book up from INR53 crores to INR66 crores in 9M, three-to-four Fortune 500 wins and a $20 million Fortune 50 deal.
scores.quote: We also announced a very large Fortune 50 retailer, a $20 million deal over a four-to-five-year period that we signed up in March

scores.rationale: Customers in 49 countries (up from 47 a quarter earlier), 16 global offices, and existing clients like Abbott pulling the platform into new countries, with a five-year-old US business now winning top-tier logos.
scores.quote: Or a customer like Abbott taking us to a new country

scores.rationale: Only about a third of NRR comes from contractual inflation escalators of 3-8% with the rest volume-linked (members/transactions) and headline growth heavily aided by acquisitions, though aiRA upsell is a genuine mix improvement.
scores.quote: about third of this growth comes from inflationary increases, from metric expansion

scores.rationale: Neither call frames the business or its end markets in cyclical terms; contracted multi-year subscriptions are discussed as non-cyclical recurring revenue.

Loyalty/retention marketing is a durable secular category and management credibly argues AI expands the addressable spend from platform into analytics and campaign execution, though the TAM extension is still aspirational.
scores.quote: our TAM today wa s largely in the loyalty platform... We are now expanding into the intelligence and the action spaces as well

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (net cash, ~INR1 crore finance cost) and M&A is bought counter-cyclically at distressed prices, but the strategy is explicitly serial-acquisition rather than organic, including a sizeable Mastercard carve-out.
scores.quote: The third axis of growth is the M&A machine. Again to remind everyone, we buy competitors out

scores.rationale: Founder-led for 18 years through five technology waves, building an India-headquartered global category leader and refusing to chase adjacencies outside loyalty.
scores.quote: we will obviously monetize this actively, but we'll stay in the loyalty space only. I mean the idea is not to monetize any of this outside

scores.rationale: Presentations are business-mechanics-led with no personality promotion, though the newly listed management leans heavily on analyst accolades in its self-description.
scores.quote: We are global leaders at what we do

scores.rationale: The calls discuss headcount economics (1% headcount growth on 23% revenue growth) but say nothing about talent development systems or internal leadership pipeline.

Unusually granular and self-critical disclosure — separating organic from inorganic NRR, normalising PAT for IPO/gratuity one-offs and a INR25 crore indemnity, and warning that SessionM will dilute margin percentages rather than spinning it.
scores.quote: the inorganic si de, which is the INR35 million that we bought from SessionM, right, those will not show much margins for the next 12 months

scores.rationale: Headline results (53% revenue CAGR, EBITDA -3%→14.6%) are impressive but much is acquisition-assembled with thin PAT and 3% ROCE, and the two-call public track record is too short to separate skill from a favourable roll-up arbitrage.
scores.quote: return on capital employed, we have seen a constant improvement and today stand at about 3%

scores.rationale: Within each installed account the platform is effectively the sole loyalty ledger of record with audit obligations, giving monopoly-like standing per customer, though not across the market.
scores.quote: it's almost looked at like a n active bank ledger in that sense

scores.rationale: Switching costs are the central industry fact — roughly seven to nine integrations per customer make incumbents near-immovable, which is precisely why Capillary buys rivals rather than displacing them.
scores.quote: once you go live with a loyalty platform, you have some seven, eight integrations in a customer. So, for a customer to then, you know, move, it really needs a lot of pain

scores.rationale: The market is explicitly fragmented with a long tail of sub-$50 million vendors plus agencies and mega-vendors, and Fortune 2000 buyers run six-month RFPs with heavy negotiation, so end-customer power is high.
scores.quote: given the fragmented nature of the loyalty industry, there aren't many players beyond the, you know, $50 million - $100 million in revenues

scores.rationale: Entry requires $10-20 million of annual platform reinvestment plus enterprise-grade uptime, security and integrations, which most incumbents cannot fund; pricing is contract-escalator based rather than discount-war driven, though migration discounts are routinely given.
scores.quote: most o f these platforms aren't able to continue to invest that $10 million to $20 million every year to keep the platform going

scores.rationale: The whole strategy is predicated on identifiable weak competitors — under-invested legacy platforms and delivery-heavy agencies — from whom Capillary takes customers organically and by acquisition.
scores.quote: that's a big part of why we win a lot of new customers from old agencies, clunky tech stacks which aren't able to keep up

scores.rationale: Loyalty is a narrow, data-proprietary niche that management argues generalist AI entrants ignore, though the company itself is now listed, analyst-rated and actively promoted.
scores.quote: loyalty is very niche, right? So I think there's also a lot of very proprietary data that ends up getting generated in a loyalty stack

scores.rationale: High and rising gross margin near 70% with sticky compounding demand and accepted annual price escalators, but pricing power comes from lock-in and usage metrics rather than brand image or taste.
scores.quote: our gross margins are around the 69 %-70% now. So it is a high gro ss margin software business

scores.rationale: The product is sold on certainty — five-nines uptime, auditable point ledgers holding real currency, and enterprise governance/privacy investment — with reliability explicitly placed above AI fuzziness.
scores.quote: A lot of our customers run annual audits, so it can't be a fuzzy AI -led system

scores.rationale: Deep touchpoint integration, fast three-to-six month go-lives versus two years for rivals, 16 global offices and a ramped US enterprise sales force give real accessibility, though not an unmatched service network.
scores.quote: it take s anything between I'd say 3 months to 6-7 months to go live. And that's actually very fast in a loyalty conte xt, usually people take like two years with some of our competitors

scores.rationale: The benefit set is correctly matched to a near-pure corporate base — 97% of revenue from large enterprises buying reliability, auditability and TCO with integration-driven lock-in rather than brand appeal.
scores.quote: 97% of our revenues come from very large enterprise customers

scores.rationale: Multi-product AI-native stack rated 5 on 5 across 22 of 27 Forrester criteria, backed by ~20% of revenue R&D intensity and an AI-led migration tool that shortens acquisition integration to a two-to-four week UAT.
scores.quote: Out of the 27 criteria that Forrester has for loyalty, we have a 5 on 5 on 22. I think that's probably the highest

scores.rationale: There is genuine data scale — 1.9 billion consumer profiles and 10 billion annual transactions feeding the analytics agent — but it is a data advantage within single-tenant accounts, not a self-reinforcing two-sided network.
scores.quote: Given the depth of data that we hav e across customers, right? 1.9 billion consumers, over 10 billion transactions every year

scores.rationale: Reach is adequate — 16 offices, 49 countries and analyst-report lead generation into Fortune 2000 CMOs — but distribution is not a rival-proof advantage against mega-vendor competitors and is still being built out in the US.
scores.quote: the US business is still only five years old

scores.rationale: Large, self-funded growth capex (₹900cr over 5 years, ₹1,000cr programme, 17 injectable lines) with fixed-asset turnover of 3.91x, but management concedes repeated project delays and topline has risen only ~50% while fixed assets doubled, so incremental returns are still unproven.
scores.quote: Investment in capex stands at INR 900 crore s in the last five years

scores.rationale: Only nascent branded-generic/brand-marketing initiatives in Central America and the Dominican Republic are mentioned, with no disclosed A&P spend or evidence of durable brand equity.
scores.quote: We are also getting into Brand Marketing in Dominican Republic, Guatemala, and Nicaragua

scores.rationale: R&D crossed 5% of turnover and ₹100cr for the first time in FY26 and is visibly productive — 60 ANDAs, 10 approvals in four quarters, first-cycle approvals and 14-15 month approval timelines versus ~20 months industry.
scores.quote: our approval timelines are between 14 to 15 months on average compared to industry timelines of about 20 months

scores.rationale: Deals are small complementary bolt-ons (₹25cr Vizag API asset purchase, ~15 acquired ANDAs, a targeted LatAm distributor) funded from cash, with management explicitly rejecting scale-for-its-own-sake, though the acquired API plant has slipped repeatedly.
scores.quote: going for the sake of acquisition, I would not advise us to go for actually acquisition without going for a meaningful acquisition. That will be a vanity

scores.rationale: Asked directly how it would prioritise higher shareholder payouts against capex and M&A, management answered entirely in terms of reinvestment and acquisitions, with no buyback or articulated distribution policy across the 16 calls despite ₹1,471cr of free cash.
scores.quote: How does management is going to prioritize between the inorganic opportunities and the incremental capex and the higher shareholder payouts?

scores.rationale: Fixed-asset turnover of 3.91x is decent and the US front-end is deliberately asset-light, but the model is working-capital heavy by design (six months of stock near customers, 121-136 day receivables) and the asset base is being expanded far ahead of revenue.
scores.quote: we always keep the goods in our subsidiary warehouses for a minimum of six -months stock

scores.rationale: Concrete share capture from a small base — 41% shelf space in Central American independent pharmacies with a path to 57%, recently launched US products "garnering higher market share quarter on quarter", and a US own-label that reached ~₹100cr in its first full year.
scores.quote: we found out that the shelf space for Caplin products are 41% in these individual pharmacies

scores.rationale: Sustained, delivered geographic build-out over the period: Chile (135 registrations, $10m order book), Mexico tender wins and a planned plant, new warehouses in Chile and Guatemala, plus a US front end with 45-50 state licences and 54 non-US regulated filings.
scores.quote: We have 135 -products to the tune of $10 million for the next 18 months to be supplied

scores.quote: COGS as a percentage of revenue has come down from 43% to 39%

scores.rationale: The only cyclical signal is management's 2022 view that generic injectable price erosion had bottomed; there is no identifiable cycle trough the company is positioned against.
scores.quote: the price erosion that has happened in the market even in injectables, I would say, has largely bottomed out

scores.rationale: End markets show secular support — persistent worldwide shortages in prefilled syringes and lyophilisation capacity and rising affordable-medicine demand at the LatAm bottom of the pyramid — though generics overall are a price-eroding, not permanently expanding, value pool.
scores.quote: there is only a shortage of capacity around the world for pre -fill syringes

scores.rationale: Virtually debt-free with ₹1,471cr cash, every project funded from internal accruals, no large acquisitions and continued counter-cyclical factory building through volatile periods.
scores.quote: Cash -Rich and Zero Leverage... INR 1,471 crores in cash

scores.rationale: A decade-plus turnaround executed on a deliberately contrarian path (LatAm bottom-of-pyramid, smaller US wholesalers rather than the big three), with the chairman relocating next to the plant to supervise projects personally.
scores.quote: targeting the smaller warehouses and IDMs rather t han the big 3

scores.rationale: The business operates in unglamorous markets, but the chairman's calls are heavily rhetorical and self-referential, including ranking comparisons and claims of being number one in the state.
scores.quote: Today, we are the number one company in Tamil Nadu

scores.rationale: Systematic people investment — training managers for attrition, senior hires from Olam and ex-INVIMA inspectors, video SOPs in regional languages to institutionalise knowledge — but management also admits it struggles to retain project talent in Tamil Nadu.

scores.rationale: Results are backed by hard evidence (80% PAT-to-CFO conversion, tripled liquid assets), but the narrative is heavily philosophical and the analyst-flagged gap between doubled fixed assets and 10-11% revenue growth tempers attributing outcomes purely to skill.
scores.quote: your fixed assets, these have doubled in last 2.5 to 3 years, but our top line is up by only 50%

scores.rationale: Caplin has built an entrenched position in niches large players ignore — deliberate 'value monopoly' in LatAm bottom-of-pyramid markets backed by 41% pharmacy shelf share — though this is share strength rather than a true monopoly.
scores.quote: it's time for a company like us to create the value monopoly in areas where the big boys do not have their playground

scores.quote: This might take up to 15 months for you to change the plans

scores.rationale: Sterile injectable manufacturing is a concentrated, capital-intensive field with few credible players, and in some LatAm niches the company chooses products with minimal competition.
scores.quote: there are hardly three or four companies who woul d have 16 or 17 -lines of injectable actually in India

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are high (USFDA/EU GMP compliance, multi-year approvals, hundreds of crores of capex) and pricing has been described as stable with erosion bottomed out, though generics remain structurally deflationary.

scores.rationale: Management points to older regional peers that have failed to reach even half its sales and to sub-scale 'virtual' US companies without their own ANDAs, both natural donors of share.
scores.quote: There are companies which are now 10-12 years ahead of us... Still they have not even reached 50% of our sales

scores.rationale: The entire strategy is built on unglamorous, under-covered niches — bottom-of-pyramid LatAm, small US wholesalers and IDMs rather than the big three — that larger capital deliberately avoids.
scores.quote: This one is not the mainstay for big companies, hence the focus of our business will be more on private markets

scores.quote: the gross margins going up from 55.3% to 59.6%

scores.quote: what makes company A different from company B is how good a track record of compliance and continuity of supply is going to matter

scores.rationale: Proximity to the customer is the explicit operating model — subsidiary warehouses holding six months of stock, own LatAm front end and sales teams, and weekly ordering relationships with the four largest US wholesalers.
scores.quote: we've just been disciplined with the strategy of keeping the products closest to the customer

scores.rationale: Benefit types are reasonably matched to customer mix — reliability and supply continuity for institutional tenders and US wholesalers/IDMs, and branded generics plus pharmacy shelf presence for retail buyers in Central America.
scores.quote: we also start ed a branded generic business which is increasing in 3 major countries of Central America

scores.rationale: A widening multi-format sterile platform (vials, PFS, cartridges, IV bags, ophthalmics, lyo, blow-fill-seal, onco) with first-cycle approvals for emulsions and a patent filed on video SOPs, but this is process and regulatory competence rather than proprietary technology.
scores.quote: we cover the entire gamut of sterile products

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network in the excerpts.

Distribution is the company's stated identity and hardest-to-copy asset — owned LatAm subsidiaries and warehouses built over 20 years, 50-state US licensing with its own label, and a pending distributor acquisition to reach private-market nooks and corners.
scores.quote: our U.S. presence will eventually be known for our strength in distribution and range

scores.rationale: Capex is steady and growth-oriented (~Rs.350 cr/yr guided, Rs.309 cr delivered in FY26) with genuinely new capability lines like a semiconductor wafer-fab components facility, but consolidated ROCE fell from 19.7% to 16.9%, so incremental returns are not yet high.
scores.quote: we commissioned the first module of an exclusive facility for the manufacturing of advanced components for semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment with a CAPEX outlay of INR 66 crores

scores.rationale: Only passing references to branding/go-to-market spend in abrasives, with no evidence of an A&P programme building durable brand equity or pricing power.
scores.quote: branding of established products in newer geographies, onboarding of key potential OEMs as customers

scores.rationale: R&D has produced commercialised new products — treated grains that helped double exports, SOFC ceramics for AI data centres, semiconductor components — though R&D intensity is never quantified.
scores.quote: Introduction of treated grains, coupled with anti-dumping duties against Chinese grains by EU, all helped to achieve this

scores.rationale: The 2022 acquisition programme has been a clear value destroyer: Rhodius (EV €55m) promised 12-14% EBIT by FY2026 but posted a €2.6m FY26 PAT loss, AWUKO promised FY2024 breakeven and is being wound up with a Rs.119 cr exceptional, and Foskor Zirconia is being closed.
scores.quote: approved to initiate the closure of Awuko through a voluntary winding-up process... exceptional items relating to this closure amounts to INR 119 crores

scores.rationale: No discussion of buybacks or distribution policy in any of the excerpts.

This is a capital-intensive multi-plant manufacturer (fused minerals, ceramics, abrasives) whose returns have been eroding rather than benefiting from asset-light economics, with consolidated ROCE down to 16.9% and segment ROCEs falling sharply.
scores.quote: return on capital employed at a consolidated level is 16.9% compared to 19.7% during the same period last year

scores.rationale: Standalone electrominerals exports doubled to a third of segment sales by displacing Chinese grains with global OEMs, and abrasives is adding dealers and OEM accounts, indicating real runway and capture.
scores.quote: Exports grew by 100% from FY25 to FY26 and currently contribute to little over 33% of the total sales, compared to 11% of the sales in FY25

scores.rationale: The overseas footprint has largely gone backwards — Germany (AWUKO wound up, Rhodius loss-making), South Africa (Foskor closing) and Russia (VAW sanctioned, sales -35%) — which outweighs solid Australia/America ceramics performance.
scores.quote: VAW recorded sales of almost 6 billion roubles compared to 9.4 billion roubles in FY25. This marks a decline of 35.3%

scores.rationale: Growth is repeatedly volume-led while realisations fall, in electrominerals standalone, at Foskor and under Chinese import pressure, which is the opposite of price/mix-led growth.
scores.quote: Sales volume went up substantially, 28% growth. At the same time, the realisation fell by 13% because of the price pressure from Chinese competition

scores.rationale: FY26 shows a trough-to-recovery pattern — weak H1 from dealer destocking and unseasonal rains, then 14-15% H2 rebound aided by GST rationalisation, with China's abrasive export rebate removal a further tailwind ahead.
scores.quote: the business faced issues such as inventory correction from the dealer channel, unseasonal rains... implementation of GST rate rationalization and a rebound in festival season demand provided a growth impetus

scores.rationale: Genuine secular end-markets are emerging in the ceramics portfolio — SOFC demand from AI data centres, semiconductor wafer-fab components and metallised cylinders for power T&D.
scores.quote: Engineering Ceramics segment grew by 30%, driven by the SOFC segment, which is seeing a strong demand in the AI-driven data center segment

scores.rationale: Leverage discipline is exemplary (net cash standalone, consolidated D/E 0.03-0.09) but stewardship is undercut by a sizeable overseas M&A programme that had to be written off, the opposite of an organic-focus mandate.
scores.quote: There was no debt in our standalone books and total debt at a consolidated basis was Rs. 112 crores... The debt-to-equity ratio was at 0.03

scores.rationale: Management articulates a long horizon (Aspiration 2030, multi-year subsidiary turnaround plans) and did eventually take hard decisions, but tenacity was spent on four years of unsuccessful turnarounds before exiting.
scores.quote: considering the continued underperformance of the subsidiary with the mounting losses and its inability to turn around

scores.rationale: Calls are run by the MD, CFO and an IR advisor in a plain numbers-first format with no promotional framing or personality-driven narrative across the full four-year span.
scores.quote: We will begin this call by providing an overview of the Company's performance for the full year FY26 and Q4 FY26, followed by an outlook for FY27

scores.rationale: Deliberate team-building is visible — recruiting CFO/IT leadership and a dedicated integration leader for the German units, plus internal succession with the Finance & Strategy Director becoming MD.
scores.quote: We now have a dedicated leader appointed for the integration of AWUKO and Rhodius

scores.rationale: Management gives explicit segment-level guidance, then scores itself against it including the misses, and discloses subsidiary losses entity by entity rather than burying them in consolidation.
scores.quote: During the last call, we gave a sales growth of 13% to 14% in Ceramics. We achieved 9.3% growth in Ceramics

scores.rationale: Stripping out the strong FY23 cyclical results, the promise-versus-delivery record is poor — Rhodius's 12-14% EBIT by FY2026 and AWUKO's FY2024 breakeven both failed — so past results overstated managerial skill.
scores.quote: We expect the EBIT margin of 12% to 14% by FY2026... CUMI expects AWUKO to break even by FY2024

scores.rationale: Some niche positions exist (metallised cylinders for vacuum interrupters, SOFC components) but the core abrasives and electrominerals businesses face open competition and imports, so no monopoly-like hold is demonstrated.

scores.rationale: Customised engineered ceramics and OEM-qualified products carry real switching costs, evidenced by customer inspection/approval gating shipments and long-standing global OEM relationships.
scores.quote: while we have an order, the ability to ship depends on the inspection by the customers

scores.rationale: Markets are fragmented and contested rather than a stable oligopoly, with Chinese dumping repeatedly setting the price in both abrasives and electrominerals.
scores.quote: Standalone business was primarily hit due to a drop in price realisations by almost 4% to 6% due to price pressure owing to lower price imports

scores.rationale: Pricing is irrational and externally driven — the company depends on EU anti-dumping duties and Chinese policy changes rather than structural barriers, and realisations fell across segments.
scores.quote: the realisation dropped by 13%, volume went up by 22%

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are visibly exiting or retreating — AWUKO's assets were bought out of insolvency, and EU anti-dumping duties plus China's export-rebate removal open share for CUMI.

scores.rationale: The company operates in unglamorous industrial consumables niches covered by a handful of domestic brokerages, with no sign of capital or new entrants crowding in.
scores.quote: hosted by DAM Capital Advisors Limited

scores.rationale: There is little image-based pricing power — the company is a price-taker facing import-led realisation declines and had to pass on cost inflation reactively rather than lead price.
scores.quote: prices are soft and that is why it starts reflecting it in the PBIT margin

scores.rationale: Customers buy certified reliability — best-in-class disc quality, high-purity powders and precision machining for semiconductor equipment, and OEM relationships that carried the export ramp.
scores.quote: Exports were driven by leveraging business existing relationships with many global OEMs across Abrasives and Refractories

scores.rationale: Domestic reach is a real asset, with the H2 recovery explicitly driven by dealer appointment and go-to-market expansion rather than price.

scores.rationale: The mix is predominantly corporate/industrial where CUMI does offer reliability and switching-cost lock-in, but the retail abrasives side lacks the intangible brand pull the framework wants, leaving it merely adequate.
scores.quote: the growth was majorly driven by the industrial and retail segment where the major growth is coming from volume increase

scores.rationale: A credible multi-product technology edge exists in ceramics and grains — high-purity powders to precision machining, treated grains, SOFC — though it is confined to part of the portfolio.
scores.quote: end-to-end capability from preparation of high purity powders to precision machining

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the calls.

scores.quote: CUMI will gain access to the coated abrasive capacity in Europe with global distribution base

scores.rationale: Capex is barely discussed across four years — growth comes from an asset-light franchise/platform model (abSure franchises, 350+ locations) rather than owned physical expansion, so incremental returns are high but there is no evidence of high and rising growth capex.
scores.quote: There are 350-plus physical locations now for us.

scores.rationale: A&P is deliberately near-zero yet brand equity keeps compounding — organic traffic rose from 84% in FY23 to 95% by FY26 with Google Trends dominance — which is extremely high A&P efficiency, though it reflects restraint rather than brand-building spend.
