scores.rationale: A dividend exists and was cut from 140% to 90% in the downturn — prudent but reactive, with no buybacks or articulated distribution policy.
scores.quote: Board has decided to reduce the dividend from 140% to 90% subject to shareholders' approval

scores.rationale: This is a heavy, backward-integrated foundry (coke, sponge iron, pig iron, ferroalloys, coal blocks) whose plants are running at ~50% capacity in FY26 — the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: the industry running at 50% capacity

scores.rationale: Share is roughly static at 20-25% of the domestic market while capacity floods in from Jai Balaji, Tata Steel and Shyam Metalics; management's stated ambition is to 'maintain' leadership rather than capture share.
scores.quote: We have around 20%-25% of the domestic market.

scores.rationale: Exports are a genuine, decades-old franchise with ten overseas subsidiaries, and export volumes grew 11% Q-o-Q and 7% in FY26 while domestic collapsed — but the concentration is risky, with ~50% of exports into a Middle East now disrupted by the US-Iran conflict.
scores.quote: we are the largest exporters into the Middle Eastern market, even if you take into consideration the Chinese

scores.rationale: Growth has been purely volume/capacity-led with realizations set by tenders and raw-material pass-through; in FY26 pricing collapsed outright, with management calling it an 'NSR collapse' driven by demand-supply mismatch.
scores.quote: it has reduced the demand so substantially, I think which has created a practically NSR collapse

scores.rationale: The company is demonstrably at the trough — volumes down 25% in FY26, EBITDA margin down to 9.4% from 17% — with an identifiable catalyst in JJM 2.0's Rs.8.69 lakh crore outlay and enquiries already restarting.
scores.quote: In my opinion, most definitely this is not the new normal, this is the rock bottom.

scores.rationale: The underlying drivers (urbanization, aging pipe replacement, irrigation, river linking) are genuinely secular, but FY26 proved the demand is not structural in practice — it is a single government programme that can be switched off overnight.
scores.quote: JJM constituted 50%-60% of the industry's total demand and we never expected that due to some irregularities, we will be in a position where there will be such a strong and such a sudden handbrake

scores.rationale: Leverage has been reduced consistently through the cycle — standalone gross debt from Rs.2,010cr (FY24) to Rs.1,202cr (FY26), net debt/equity 0.31 — with land bought from internal accruals and bank commitments explicitly prioritized over expansion.
scores.quote: Whatever commitment we have made with the bankers we will meet the commitments first, then we will process fund for acquisition of the land

scores.rationale: A consistent multi-decade thesis on water executed through capacity build-out and a two-decade export presence, held to through the FY26 downturn without panic.
scores.quote: We always thought that water is the business of the future and we are in the right place at the right time

scores.rationale: Low-key, no-hype tone throughout — early calls were fronted by finance staff, and management repeatedly refuses to give figures until firm rather than talk up projects.
scores.quote: there is no point in sharing a figure with you today and changing it tomorrow

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline; the board is dominated by eight Kejriwal-family and related MDs with no stated internal-promotion process.

Management disclosed the Rs.60cr Khardah repair and 53-day shutdown, the Rs.38cr labour-law provision, and openly corrected an investor's overstatement of the fund release from Rs.15,000cr to Rs.1,500cr against their own interest.
scores.quote: Just a correction, sir, the disbursement that was done last year was not INR 15,000 crores, it was INR 1,500 crores

scores.rationale: The FY24 boom (PAT +134%, EBITDA margin 17%) and the FY26 bust (PAT Rs.161cr, margin 9.4%) were both driven by JJM budget flows rather than management skill, so results reveal little about capability.
scores.quote: we were quite certain that, that is also not a normal, that is the upper end, here we are at the lower end

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position — pipes are sold via competitive tender to EPC contractors on price, with management conceding all producers use identical inputs and pricing moves together.
scores.quote: we generally the entire DI pipe industry are operating on same raw material, everything is same

scores.rationale: No switching costs or captive aftermarket; there is not even material product stickiness, with OPVC, steel and plastic pipes competing for the same applications.
scores.quote: we have lot of types of pipes in the market, we have ductile, we have steel, we have some different types of plastics

scores.rationale: Industry capacity is expanding from 46-48 lakh tonnes to ~57 lakh tonnes with new entrants Jai Balaji, Tata Steel and Shyam Metalics, and the single dominant customer (government/EPC) holds all the negotiating power.
scores.quote: we estimate it around 57 lakh tonnes in 25-26

scores.rationale: Capacity poured in just as demand halved, producing exactly the discount war the framework warns against — stock swelled at every supplier, prices collapsed and, in the CEO's words, everybody is in business trouble.
scores.quote: the stock swelled with every supplier. So everybody came under a cash crunch and a business issue

scores.rationale: The FY26 stress leaves weaker, sub-scale and cash-crunched DI producers vulnerable, and Electrosteel's cash of ~Rs.800cr and low debt position it to take that share on recovery.
scores.quote: Practically, everybody is in business trouble.

scores.rationale: The opposite of ignored — the DI pipe opportunity was widely written up and drew capital from Tata Steel, Jai Balaji and Shyam Metalics into the same capacity build.
scores.quote: we read a number of reports about how the opportunity in Ductile Iron Pipe for many, many years was going to be extremely strong

scores.rationale: Zero pricing power from image — realization is set by demand-supply and raw material pass-through, and gross profit fell 1,222 bps Y-o-Y once demand softened.
scores.quote: It's just a demand-supply mismatch.

scores.rationale: Some reliability value exists via country-specific coatings/approvals and a small export premium for stringent specifications, but management concedes export pricing is essentially the same as domestic — price, not trust, sets the deal.
scores.quote: Certain specific countries have more stringent requirements, so they allow you to derive a small premium. But overall, it would be similar to the domestic market

scores.rationale: Ten overseas subsidiaries operating on a stock-and-sale basis give real local availability and repeat demand, and management cites the distribution network as a stated strategic advantage.
scores.quote: because of our permanent presence, it helps us in serving the customers there

scores.rationale: The customer is government-funded EPC contractors buying on tender price — a corporate customer with no switching-cost lock-in, and the FY26 collapse showed how completely that customer controls terms.
scores.quote: we are supplying to EPC players

scores.rationale: No technology edge is claimed anywhere; capacity is added with commodity 'balancing equipment' and even valve production is described as development work just beginning.
scores.quote: We have already started the development work for Valvecastings in India and look forward to production soon.

scores.rationale: No network effects are present or discussed in this business model.

Two decades of established overseas subsidiaries across Europe, UK, US, Middle East and Singapore delivered a genuine cushion when domestic collapsed, making it the firm's most defensible asset — though the Middle East concentration limits it.
scores.quote: our integrated manufacturing operations and strong distribution network continue to provide us with strategic advantages

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex into an integrated campus with two new factories plus strategic backward integration (foundry, motors, pressure vessels) that management links to competitiveness rather than mere maintenance, though ROCE targets slipped on working capital.
scores.quote: we are in the process of shifting our city campus progressively over the last next probably six years... two factories are being set up there

scores.rationale: Deliberate, rising A&P to build brand pull in under-penetrated markets and a go-to-market project to find new customers, but the payoff is still described as pending.
scores.quote: our brand being less well known requires a lot more investment at the top of the funnel, marketing enablers, brand pull

scores.rationale: R&D has repeatedly converted into commercial wins across the period — PG850 portables, super-premium two-stage machines, own dryers, Demand=Match, and an in-house motor program built with almost no capital that became a structural cost/quality advantage.
scores.quote: We didn't make any investments other than some testing equipment... today that's become another huge strategic pillar for us, a competitive advantage

scores.rationale: Roughly six-seven acquisitions whose integration management itself judges inefficient, and the acquired distribution (Patton's/Michigan Air) and Rotair businesses remain below target or margin-dilutive years later.
scores.quote: We did, I think six or seven acquisitions... I think we could have been a lot more efficient and effective

scores.rationale: No discussion of buybacks, dividend policy or any distribution framework in the excerpts.

Cash conversion and working-capital discipline are strong, but deliberate backward integration into foundry, motors and pressure vessels plus a new multi-year campus make the model more asset-heavy, not asset-light.
scores.quote: We do strategic, selective, backward integration... Foundry, motor production, our own pressure vessel

scores.rationale: Small global share leaves a long runway and share capture is demonstrated across geographies — India share gains across all product segments, distributor conversions in the US, new distributors and Sydney gains in Australia.
scores.quote: we've doubled our sales capacity... this has effectively helped convert a lot of distributors from competition to our fold

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-year international build-out with 17% ISAAME and 22% Europe five-year CAGRs and a Middle East channel-to-direct pivot, but Europe required restructuring to reach only break-even and North America lost a year to an ERP failure.
scores.quote: we've enjoyed nearly 22% CAGR of the last five years is a testament to the quality of our execution

scores.rationale: Growth is volume, exchange and cost pass-through rather than pricing or mix — FY26 pricing contributed almost nothing and mix-rich Demand=Match is still immaterial, echoing the 2022 admission of under-recovering input costs.
scores.quote: volume growth... was around 3 to 4 percent, right. Pricing was hardly much

scores.rationale: Several exposures are explicitly at cycle bottoms with identified upturns ahead — US portables at the bottom of a three-year cycle, water-well in paralysis, and Indian capex inquiries recovering.
scores.quote: Our leader who runs that business believes we're at the bottom of a three-year cycle

scores.rationale: Compressed air is a utility tied to broad industrial capacity addition with no single-industry dependence, aided by US reshoring and Indian industrialisation, but it tracks industrial cycles rather than a permanent secular boom.
scores.quote: compressed air is a utility, just like electricity. So, when your capacity goes up in a factory... you need more compressed air

scores.rationale: Consistently organic in recent years with explicit refusal of inorganic plays, a solid net-cash balance sheet, 100% EBITDA-to-cash conversion, and cost realignment rather than deal-making when Europe weakened.
scores.quote: We are not looking at any inorganic play in Germany at this point in time, or in Europe at this point in time

scores.rationale: A decades-long, independently pursued arc — 1992 redirection, 2013 global push, 25 years building manufacturing quality — with the vacuum entry framed as a 10-12 year program rather than a near-term revenue play.
scores.quote: it's a 10-to-12-year program. This is not something that we can go tomorrow and start looking at huge growth

scores.rationale: Coimbatore-based, understated tone with self-deprecating framing of its own niche and no celebrity posturing, though the company now runs high-visibility annual investor meets in Mumbai.
scores.quote: for us who are at the bottom of the market any turbulence at the top of the surface is irrelevant

scores.rationale: Systematic capability building with heavy investment in leadership and platforms, regional leaders given the stage, and India-developed talent redeployed to the Middle East, though much of the bench is newly assembled.
scores.quote: We are investing quite heavily in building competencies to take the company to the next level

scores.rationale: Every call opens with an unprompted EBITDA bridge explaining the shortfall, and management openly owns failures — the ERP-driven lost year, the commodity-price blindsiding, the acquisition inefficiency, and investor-feedback lapses.
scores.quote: The last time we were kind of blindsided, we didn't watch this carefully and we took a hit on our profitability

scores.rationale: Management actively separates luck from skill, attributing the FY23 US peak to post-COVID buying conditions rather than execution and flagging cyclical segments as outside their control.
scores.quote: we were still sort of enjoying the post COVID hangover, record prices record volume increases

scores.rationale: Dominance exists only in narrow pockets such as Indian portables, while in the core industrial market ELGi is a challenger that must hunt for new customers rather than owning the customer's mind.
scores.quote: The challenge is to go out and find new customers

scores.rationale: Real switching-cost inertia in the installed base plus a captive multi-brand service/aftermarket stream, and structurally protected pricing in remote Australia.
scores.quote: there is a general tendency to stick with what you have... unless the existing manufacturer has done very badly, the tendency is to rinse and repeat

scores.rationale: A globally stable structure among a handful of established players with fragmented industrial end customers who lack negotiating power, though the low-kW segment is being churned by Chinese entrants.
scores.quote: The overall industry structure is pretty much stable, not only in India, but in the rest of the world

scores.rationale: Pricing at the premium end stays rational and cost increases are passed on industry-wide, but low-cost Chinese entrants are visibly attacking the entry segment in every market, forcing a defensive product launch.
scores.quote: we see a significant influx of lower priced Chinese products in in the lower kilowatt price driven sector

scores.rationale: Weak or constrained rivals are actively donating share — US distributors switching to ELGi, Australian distributors onboarding, and the domestic screw-compressor challenger judged far behind.
scores.quote: they do have a presence in the market, but they have a long way to go in terms of getting their products ready

scores.rationale: A prosaic, low-glamour industrial niche run from Coimbatore that management describes as beneath the notice of market turbulence and larger players.
scores.quote: it is like the fish at the bottom of the ocean, so what if there is a storm

scores.rationale: Pricing power comes from measurable efficiency rather than image, and the brand is explicitly weak enough in key markets to require funding, with commodity cost increases only partially recovered.
scores.quote: we have recovered only 40% of that

scores.rationale: The overwhelming majority of customers buy on efficiency, reliability and uptime rather than price, backed by Deming-grade quality, in-house castings and vessels for safety, and lead-time availability in mining.
scores.quote: 80% of the customers buy on efficiency and we are right up there in the world as one of the most efficient compressors

scores.rationale: Deep distributor plus direct-service coverage with rising feet-on-street and multi-brand servicing gives strong customer intimacy in India and Australia, though US and European direct reach is still being built.
scores.quote: 600 distributors out of that, only about 60 roughly are in India

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely industrial/corporate and the value proposition is correctly built on total cost of ownership, reliability and service lock-in rather than consumer-style intangibles.
scores.quote: provide energy efficiency and reliability without any compromise on either cost or total cost of ownership

scores.rationale: A genuine multi-product engineering edge in efficiency, in-house motor design and Demand=Match, but management concedes the motor advantage is replicable and Demand=Match revenue is still negligible.
scores.quote: Can a competitor, do it? They probably are already doing it, and the others can do it too

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the excerpts.

A 120-country, 600-distributor network with owned direct-sales and multi-brand service arms in the US and Australia is a real advantage in a business where service is vital, but coverage in Europe and US direct sales is still sub-scale.
scores.quote: we have a presence in over 120 countries

scores.rationale: Nearly all capex is greenfield growth capacity (1,370→1,910→2,130 TPD, three new plants, ~INR450cr programme) funded from a net-cash balance sheet, with segment EBITDA margins of 38-40% implying strong incremental returns.
scores.quote: we remain disciplined on Capex with guidance of rupees 2,500 million in FY26 and rupees 2,000 million in FY27

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend across any of the calls; it is a B2B contract-driven gases business.
No R&D spend or new-product pipeline is disclosed; the only technical capability cited is an in-house engineering team that designs and assembles ASUs from bought-in machines.
scores.quote: we design the plants, and we buy the machines from suppliers across the world, and then our internal team does the putting it all together at the site

scores.rationale: The only acquisition is a tiny, simple, genuinely complementary bolt-on (Bangalore cylinder filling, INR5.5cr) that loads the Kurnool plant, though no post-deal margin improvement has yet been demonstrated.
scores.quote: it's quite a small acquisition... the outlay is only about Rs. 5.5 crores... it's a very strategic kind of complementary acquisition

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed; IPO proceeds went to debt repayment and capex, which is capital allocation rather than distribution.

This is an explicitly asset-heavy model — INR160cr capex for a 220 TPD plant yielding roughly INR100-110cr of revenue at full ramp (≈0.7x), with management itself calling the business capital-intensive, though long-term contracts do protect returns.
scores.quote: We are also conscious that industrial gases is a capital-intensive business

scores.rationale: At only mid-single-digit share against Linde and Inox at ~25% each, the runway is large, and share is being taken from the unorganised sector plus new geographies.
scores.quote: we have a market share currently of, I would say, about 4 odd percent... which means that there is a lot of room for us to grow

scores.rationale: A credible, funded East/South-to-North/West pan-India build-out is underway (Uluberia 2 commissioned, North India H2 FY27, West-central FY28), but execution has slipped by a couple of months on at least one project and the West plant is still years out.
scores.quote: we felt this is the right time to embark on this pan India expansion

scores.rationale: Growth is fundamentally capacity/volume-led with pricing a headwind (argon realisations fell over 25% in Q3), offset only by a favourable mix shift toward higher-value argon and on-site contracts.
scores.quote: The Argon prices have declined in the last quarter by more than 25%

scores.rationale: The steel-linked argon cycle bottomed in Q3 FY26 and had begun recovering by Q4, with management expecting further normalisation into FY27 — a plausible position near a cyclical trough.
scores.quote: In Q4, we saw argon prices recover from the Q3 lows. This recovery is encouraging, and we feel that there is scope for further normalization in FY27

scores.rationale: Industrial gases are a direct proxy for Indian manufacturing capex, with a ~INR15,000cr market growing ~10% p.a. and new secular pools opening in solar, electronics, pharma and healthcare.
scores.quote: the market available to kind of the gas industry... was somewhere in the region of about 15,000 crores and it was growing at about 10 odd percent

scores.rationale: Organic greenfield growth only, INR210cr of borrowings repaid immediately post-IPO leaving net cash of INR3,550mn, and no large M&A — capital allocation is explicitly framed around discipline and return profile.
scores.quote: net cash is at 3,550 million and we remain disciplined on Capex

scores.rationale: A decades-old family business that bought out its Japanese partner and competes against MNCs on self-designed plants and 15-year contracts, framing capacity decisions on a multi-year rather than quarterly horizon.
scores.quote: that's actually one of our main strengths as an independent gas company which is not linked to one of the larger multinational groups

scores.rationale: Newly listed, sober and unpromotional tone with no self-congratulation, though the recent IPO and stated desire for brand visibility slightly reduce the obscurity.
scores.quote: The company is a lot more visible as a brand, especially post IPO

scores.rationale: Beyond noting a capable in-house project engineering team fully absorbed by internal projects, there is no discussion of talent development or a leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: our project engineering team is currently fully engaged in execution of our internal projects

scores.rationale: Management volunteered a weak quarter without spin, itemised each one-off with amounts, and owned the project delay rather than burying it.
scores.quote: it is fair to acknowledge that this was a tougher quarter sequentially. Revenue from operations declined 9% quarter on quarter

scores.rationale: Reported delivery has lagged the 20-25% CAGR promise (FY26 core gases growth 14.2%, 9M growth ~10%) and margins swing with argon prices, so results reflect cycle and commissioning timing at least as much as managerial skill.
scores.quote: Core gas's growth is around 10% for 9 months versus your 20 to 25% CAGR target

scores.rationale: On-site plants sited inside customer premises on 15-year take-or-pay contracts create a captive, effectively monopolistic supply position, though this covers only part of the book.
scores.quote: We have a 15-year contract with the customer

scores.rationale: Merchant economics are inherently regional (a ~500km radius) and clusters plus in-plant pipelines create real switching costs, but the merchant business still faces direct MNC competition on price.
scores.quote: we set up a plant, and we market it to the production to, let's say, 300, 400 customers over a 500-kilometer radius

scores.rationale: The organised market is a stable oligopoly of Linde, Inox, Air Products and Ellenbarrie, though large steel customers retain leverage and captive plants can dump surplus argon into the market.
scores.quote: Linde and Inox would each be at, I mean, somewhere close to about 25% each

scores.rationale: Capital intensity and long equipment lead times are genuine barriers, but pricing rationality broke down in Q3 with captive-plant argon oversupply, and investors flagged new ASU supply pressuring prices.
scores.quote: an oversupply of argon into the market from captive gas plants operated by steel manufacturers

scores.rationale: Management explicitly identifies the unorganised sector as the pool from which share will be taken, alongside overall market growth.
scores.quote: Growth will be driven by of course unorganized sector where we can take market from

scores.rationale: The company was under-the-radar historically but a July 2025 IPO, analyst coverage and heavy MNC capital in the sector mean it is no longer ignored.
scores.quote: This is the first call post listing of the company's shares on major stock exchanges

scores.rationale: Margins are high (38.4% gases segment in FY26) but the products are commodity air gases whose realisations swing with the steel cycle, so there is no image- or taste-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: the gases segment EBITDA margins, if we adjust for the one-off items, touched 40% in Q4

scores.rationale: The entire customer proposition is reliability and certainty of supply — most starkly in medical oxygen where proximity and dependability, not price, decide the sale.
scores.quote: Customers need assurance of supply. They need consistency. They need safety.

scores.rationale: Proximity is a deliberate strategy — local cylinder filling in Bangalore, cluster density and existing relationships that management expects to speed the Uluberia 2 ramp — but reach still trails the larger MNCs.
scores.quote: having a local cylinder filling station in Bangalore will allow us to cater to those kinds of customers

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/industrial and the model is correctly matched — long-dated take-or-pay contracts and in-plant pipelines that lock in reliability-driven buyers.
scores.quote: our business is primarily driven by long-term contracts

scores.rationale: In-house plant design and assembly is a real competence for an independent player, but there is no R&D intensity or multi-product technology edge, and core machinery is bought from third-party suppliers.
scores.quote: We have our own in-house team who keep track of the global developments in terms of production technology

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the calls.

Regional density across merchant, packaged and on-site channels gives genuine last-mile service reach in East and South India, but the network is regional and materially smaller than competitors five times its size.
scores.quote: We want a balanced portfolio across merchant, packaged, and on-site gases

scores.rationale: Capex is barely discussed across the four years — manufacturing is largely outsourced and 'investment' is described as distribution manpower/towns and consultant-led supply-chain work, not high-ROIC growth capex.
scores.quote: Third -party. Anyway, it was manufactured by a third -party, we will continue with that.

scores.rationale: A&P is sustained and counter-cyclical (up 21% in Q1FY25, up 12% in a quarter when EBITDA fell 15%, ~22-23% of sales, 50% digital), but the payoff is unproven since FY26 revenue still declined 1% and analysts openly questioned the spend level.
scores.quote: despite which we invested behind advertising and promotional spends, which grew by 12% in this quarter

scores.rationale: There is a steady stream of line extensions (Dermicool Her, Dermicool soap, Smart & Handsome sunscreen/deo, digital-first Zandu SKUs) and two WHO-GMP units, but these remain small (digital portfolio ~INR25 crore) and R&D has not created a needle-moving new franchise in four years.
scores.quote: the kind of product d evelopment capabilities we have from an R&D perspective would be unmatched

scores.rationale: A steady run of small bolt-ons (Dermicool, The Man Company, Brillare, Axiom, IncNut) that are complementary, but several were acquired loss-making or stagnant and the aggregate was EBITDA-negative, with only Axiom described as already profitable.
scores.quote: Axiom is already a profitable entity, unlike many of the new age start -ups

scores.rationale: A consistent, generous dividend policy (INR10/share in 9M FY26 including a 600% second interim) on a debt-free balance sheet, though no buyback discipline at low valuations is evidenced.
scores.quote: second interim dividend of 600%, amounting to INR6 per share for FY '26

scores.rationale: Asset-light model with third-party manufacturing, ~70% gross margin, 33% EBITDA margin, a debt-free balance sheet and a deliberate 10-day working-capital improvement, though large acquired intangibles (INR23 crore quarterly amortisation) dilute returns.
scores.quote: we consciously reduced our receivables by over INR100 crores during the year, a 10 days improvement in the working capital cycle

scores.rationale: Management cites low category penetration and unorganised players turning unviable as a share opportunity, but the four-year record shows Kesh King, Male Grooming and BoroPlus flat-to-declining and FY26 revenue down 1%, so share capture is claimed more than demonstrated.
scores.quote: the unorganized trade... they have become unviable. So that is one of the reasons why suddenly there is a spurt in organized hair oil businesses

scores.rationale: International has a real footprint (MENA, SAARC, CIS, Creme 21, Bangladesh automation of 130,000 outlets) and grew ~10-11% in good years, but it is repeatedly derailed by external shocks — Russia/Ukraine, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh currency, and a 5% Q4 FY26 decline from Hormuz disruption.
scores.quote: Our international business declined by 5% during the quarter, primarily due to geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly volume- and season-led rather than price/mix-led — 8.7% volume within 10% value in Q1FY25, explicit reluctance to take price, and GST cuts passed through as grammage increases on ~20% of the portfolio; premium mix (TMC/Brillare/IncNut) is still only ~21% of business.
scores.quote: So Harit, yes this year we will not be very aggressive with o ur price increases.

scores.rationale: The company is visibly near a cyclical trough — FY26 revenue down 1% on a failed summer, summer portfolio down 22% with talc down 40% — against a low base, GST 2.0 rate cuts to 5% and early rural recovery signalling an identifiable upturn.
scores.quote: This decline was primarily driven by weak summer rather than any structural or compet itive weakness

scores.rationale: Some end markets are secular (ayurveda/healthcare, male grooming, quick-commerce, personalised beauty) but core categories are not — management concedes the premium hair-fall oil market has been in decline and talc/prickly heat are weather-dependent.
scores.quote: the market for hair oil, particularly the premium hair fall segment, hair oil market is on a decline for quite some time now

scores.rationale: Prudent on leverage (debt-free, working capital tightened) and willing to invest counter-cyclically in A&P, but the period is marked by repeated inorganic bets — Dermicool, Helios/TMC, Brillare, Axiom, IncNut — rather than an organic focus.
scores.quote: With healthy margins and debt -free balance sheet and a portfolio that spans both across essential and premium growth categories

scores.rationale: There is tenacity in multi-year projects (Project Khoj rural expansion, 50-year franchise, persistent Kesh King revival that finally produced two double-digit quarters), but strategy is visibly outsourced to consultants — BCG for brands, KPMG for supply chain, a Bain partner hired as Chief Growth Officer.
scores.quote: we are re -working on the strategy for Kesh King and we have roped in BCG to develop the long-term strategy

scores.rationale: The Goenka family management is low-profile and calls are run by functional presidents (sales, healthcare, international, finance) answering detail rather than by promoter self-promotion.
scores.quote: MR. GUL RAJ BHATIA – PRESIDENT – HEALTH CARE... MR. MANISH GUPTA – PRESIDENT SALES

scores.rationale: Bench-building is real but predominantly bought in rather than grown — a Bain partner as Chief Growth Officer, a Dabur executive as beverages CEO — alongside genuine field-force build-out of 453 rural staff; top-level family MD churn (three MD exits in five years) offsets the pipeline story.
scores.quote: we have some high talent who have just recently joined... So I always wanted to -- we had always wanted to build a great team.

scores.rationale: Management consistently owns bad news without spin — admitting the strategic-investment portfolio was loss-making, quantifying the summer hit, and conceding brand declines rather than reframing them.
scores.quote: Overall everything put together it is still negative.

scores.rationale: There is little halo to strip away because results themselves are modest, and management repeatedly attributes good quarters to weather and bad ones to the same, which makes the skill component hard to isolate.
scores.quote: this season, we benefited from summer no doubt

scores.rationale: Emami owns several category-defining niches that occupy the customer's mind — Navratna cooling oil, Zandu balm/ayurveda and Dermicool as the prickly-heat powder — with Zandu cited as a top-of-mind ayurvedic brand.
scores.quote: It's a specific prickly heat powder... In the ayurvedic space, Zandu would be among the top leading players in terms of the consumer perception

scores.rationale: There are no switching costs or captive aftermarket in mass FMCG — sales swing with consumer and trade promotions, showing customers move freely.
scores.quote: depending on the consumer pro motions, the market behaves like that. So in a year, we do two promotions.

scores.rationale: Some niches are near-uncontested and competitive intensity in Kesh King's segment eased, but the main categories face Marico, Dabur, Patanjali and Indulekha, and adjacent bets face far worse (Campa entering beverages).
scores.quote: We have particularly Indulekha and Patanjali are main competitors. There, we are seeing intensity coming down.

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and pricing is not fully rational — e-commerce is the least profitable channel purely because of promotions, growth depends on twice-yearly consumer promotions, and new entrants like Campa have reshaped a category they just bought into.
scores.quote: the GT is more compared to the modern trade. The lowest is the e -commerce... only because of the promotions that we offer there

scores.rationale: Weak unorganised players are visibly ceding share as costs rise, and multinationals divesting sub-scale brands (Reckitt selling Dermicool) provide another source of donated share.
scores.quote: the unorganized trade, which because of the disruptions and costs going up, they have become unviable

scores.rationale: Emami operates in small, unglamorous niches — prickly-heat powder, cooling oil, balms — that large players deprioritise, evidenced by Reckitt handing Dermicool over rather than competing for it.
scores.quote: The Dermicool arrangement... it's been a distribution agreement with Reckitt

scores.rationale: Gross margins near 70% and strong mass-brand equity indicate genuine intangible pricing power, but management repeatedly declines to exercise it and demand proved fragile to weather and GST disruption.
scores.quote: gross margin expanded to 70.6%, an improvement of 30 basis points

scores.rationale: In healthcare the pitch is efficacy and certification rather than price — two WHO-GMP units and a medico/doctor-detailing force build trust-based demand.
scores.quote: we had two WHO GMP manufacturing units. WHO GMP certification is very difficult to obtain.

scores.rationale: Distribution intimacy is a genuine strength — Project Khoj took rural coverage from 32,000 to a targeted 50,000 towns with field headcount up from ~900 to ~1,300, alongside an omnichannel build to 32% of domestic sales.
scores.quote: we've added around 400 -odd -- 453 people on ground, which has taken our rural footprint manpower presence from close to 900 to almost now 1,300

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail/mass consumer and the benefit offered is correctly intangible-brand-led, now extended to younger digital consumers via 50% digital media and 30%+ organized-channel salience.
scores.quote: our 50% of our communication is digital. So we are targeting the new consumers, particularly the youth consumers.

scores.rationale: No meaningful technology edge — the portfolio is ayurvedic/personal-care formulation with third-party manufacturing, and 'differentiation' is described in product-positioning terms rather than proprietary technology.
scores.quote: this is not like a cola drink. It is aloe vera -based fruit drink. So that is absolutely differentiated product.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business is self-reinforcing with scale; the closest thing, the Zanducare D2C platform, is a one-sided direct channel whose only claimed advantage is first-mover timing.
scores.quote: we are the first mover advantage. See not many companies have their own p latform.

scores.rationale: Reach is a real advantage — deep rural expansion, wholesale dependency structurally cut to 27%, organized channels at ~32% with quick commerce up 70%, and 130,000 outlets digitally mapped in Bangladesh.
scores.quote: Wholesale c hannel dependency has reduced to 27% of total domestic sales, reflecting the structural improvement in our channel mix

scores.rationale: Growth capex is high and rising — construction spend of ₹1,182cr in FY26 (up from ₹868cr in 9M) plus a ~₹41,000cr GDV launch pipeline on fully paid-up land — but incremental ROIC is unproven with FY26 EBITDA at negative ₹300cr and revenue recognition deferred to FY28+.
scores.quote: Construction spend during FY '26 stood at INR1,182 crores, representing approximately 71% of collections

scores.rationale: The Mumbai billboard campaign and brand re-launch translated into ~₹800cr of Citadel prelaunch in 45 days and Bangalore luxury category leadership, though no A&P quantum or efficiency is disclosed.
scores.quote: we only brought this product out in mid of February, giving us only 45 days to clock almost INR800 crores

scores.rationale: No mention of R&D spend or product/technology development in any of the three calls.

The defining transaction is the opposite of a small complementary bolt-on — a large, complex reverse merger with a distressed Indiabulls Real Estate carrying stalled projects, IBC/Section 7 litigation and land disputes, and post-deal margins collapsed to negative EBITDA and a ₹872cr PAT loss.
scores.quote: the transaction was accordingly treated as a reverse merger with NAM as accounting acquirer and EDL as accounting acquiree

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy exists; the company is a net capital consumer, taking in financing via warrant conversions and carrying ₹4,100cr gross institutional plus ₹1,121cr shareholder debt.
scores.quote: a positive financing inflow driven by warrant conversions

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-heavy: a 3,250-acre fully paid land bank, ₹14,728cr of unsold inventory and ~₹5,200cr total debt against FY26 revenue of only ₹1,732cr and negative EBITDA.
scores.quote: Combined with our 3,250-acre fully paid land bank

scores.rationale: Small base in a fragmented, consolidating market with demonstrated capture — FY26 presales up 128% YoY and over 65% of all Bangalore sales in the ₹10cr+ ticket segment.
scores.quote: Our Bangalore launches in the INR10 crores ticket size accounted for over 65% of all FY '26 sales in Bangalore in that segment

scores.rationale: Credible, deliberately sequenced entry into MMR (Worli, Juhu, Alibaug; ~₹12,000cr GDV) with early validation at Citadel, but the brand is unproven outside Bengaluru and is priced below top Mumbai developers with discounts.
scores.quote: Mumbai is also being approached as a credibility-driven expansion than a volume-led market

scores.rationale: Mix is shifting decisively to luxury villas/premium towers with real price realisation (Panvel from ₹9-10k to ₹14-15k psf; Paradiso realised ₹200cr against ₹175cr GDV), though volume also surged (area sold 206k to 1.78m sq ft) and Worli requires discounting.
scores.quote: expecting our sales price, which originally was Rs. 9,000 to Rs. 10,000, to go up to roughly Rs. 14,000 to Rs. 15,000

scores.rationale: Management describes the housing cycle as already in momentum rather than near a trough, so the company is positioned mid-to-late cycle, not at the bottom with an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: As the housing cycle continues to show momentum

scores.rationale: End markets show secular support — branded-developer consolidation in Indian housing and GCC-driven demand for institutional-grade offices — though management concedes office demand is now selective post-COVID/AI.
scores.quote: consolidation towards leading trusted brands will continue

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (0.3x net debt/equity, self-imposed ≤0.5x cap) and growth is organic on fully paid land, but this is offset by a very large, messy merger and a cost base running well ahead of revenue.
scores.quote: we want to keep our net debt levels to 0.5x or less

scores.rationale: Demonstrable tenacity in taking inherited stalled assets to completion and winning multi-year legal battles (NCLAT quashing the Canara Bank CIRP, KIADB order set aside, MIDC stay), though the merged platform's own track record is only one year long.
scores.quote: 6 previously delayed residential projects across MMR, NCR and Visakhapatnam reached handover stages, enabling more than 3,300 families to finally take possessions

scores.rationale: Promoter-fronted, brand-forward management running citywide billboard campaigns and 300m+ trophy towers, but the tone on calls is operationally grounded and self-deprecating rather than celebrity-driven.
scores.quote: We're just being a little bit humble about it that we are conscious we need to build our brand

scores.rationale: Beyond generic references to 'building our teams', there is no evidence of systematic talent development, and the five-year history shows severe senior churn — four CFOs across FY22-FY25 and an MD exit.
scores.quote: integrating and building our teams and executing in a disciplined manner

scores.rationale: Management owns the guidance miss with a specific reason, explains the loss drivers and accounting mechanics in detail, and admits to discounting in Worli — though the repeated framing of losses as 'structural, not operational' carries some spin.
scores.quote: We achieved approximately 93% of our FY '26 presales guidance... attributable to approval delays of one planned project in Bangalore

scores.rationale: The headline narrative rests on presales, GDV and a claimed ₹28,000cr project surplus that are management estimates and promises, while audited results show negative EBITDA and an ₹872cr PAT loss — results and skill are hard to separate this early.
scores.quote: an estimated project surplus of approximately Rs. 28,000 crores... based on our management estimates

scores.rationale: Embassy owns a dominant position in the mind of the Bengaluru luxury buyer (65%+ of the ₹10cr+ segment) and controls its own master-planned townships, but this is a leading brand position rather than a true monopoly.
scores.quote: established a clear category leadership position

scores.rationale: Large contiguous, fully paid land holdings (Embassy Springs, Knowledge Park, 3,250 acres) create a localised quasi-monopoly on supply in North Bengaluru, though homebuyers face no switching costs at all.
scores.quote: entirely on fully paid-up land already within the platform

scores.rationale: Indian residential development is fragmented and competitive — management concedes NCR is dominated by other large players and that it must price below top Worli developers — with buyers holding real negotiating power.
scores.quote: we're not shying away from discounts

scores.rationale: Real barriers exist in land, approvals and capital (RERA delays cost them a launch), but pricing rationality is weak in the markets they are entering, where they compete on discounts and value positioning.
scores.quote: we are coming in much lower than what I think the top developers are

scores.rationale: The industry is full of weak, stalled developers to take share from — the company literally absorbed one (Indiabulls Real Estate) and is now reviving its abandoned sites at higher prices.
scores.quote: when we had stepped in, there were almost only 50 people at the site doing construction work. Today, there are more than 1,500 construction workers

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar: a heavily marketed listed platform with Blackstone as a major shareholder, a citywide Mumbai billboard campaign, marquee 300m+ towers and highly publicised IBC/ASM proceedings.
scores.quote: Many of you would have seen billboards across the city

scores.rationale: The Embassy name carries genuine pricing power in Bengaluru — Paradiso realised ₹200cr against a ₹175cr GDV estimate — but gross margins are thin at the reported level and the brand still needs discounts in Mumbai.
scores.quote: achieved realizations of approximately Rs. 200 crores against an estimated GDV of Rs. 175 crores

scores.rationale: In a market scarred by stalled projects, buyers are paying for delivery certainty and management is explicitly building the franchise on that, having handed over 3,300 delayed homes and engaged a top-tier contractor for Citadel.
scores.quote: institutional credibility is built through delivery and through taking responsibility for inherited commitments

scores.rationale: Absorption speed (₹804cr at Greenshore in five days, 87% at Verde Phase 2 in a quarter) implies an effective sales channel, but no distinct distribution reach or customer-intimacy advantage is described.
scores.quote: recorded pre-sales of approximately Rs. 804 crores within five days of launch

scores.rationale: The mix is sensibly matched — image/lifestyle intangibles sold to retail luxury homebuyers, and institutional-grade, location-specific assets built for corporate GCC office occupiers.
scores.quote: right asset, right location, and right size as well to cater to these GCCs

scores.rationale: No technology, proprietary process or R&D-driven advantage is discussed anywhere in the calls.
There is ecosystem adjacency (Embassy REIT as a potential buyer of completed assets, Embassy Group tenant relationships) but nothing self-reinforcing or two-sided that strengthens with scale.
scores.quote: We had a thought about forward purchasing it with Embassy REIT

scores.rationale: Presence across 8 cities and 40+ projects gives scale, but nothing in the calls suggests a distribution or service reach rivals cannot replicate — indeed Mumbai is being entered from scratch.
scores.quote: These will be our first residential developments under the Embassy brand in Mumbai

scores.rationale: Four new plants were operationalized in FY24 and capacity plus front-end investment was framed as a growth lever, with margins recovering (19.4% FY26, +80bps) as leverage played out, but incremental ROIC is asserted rather than demonstrated and D&A rose to INR415cr.
scores.quote: we have made investments in both our front end - through field force addition and in manufacturing capacities by operationalizing four new facilities

scores.rationale: Deliberate front-loaded investment in new brand-building franchises (Emcutix derma, Arth consumer wellness) with management accepting an 18-24 month gestation, and prescriber-level scientific promotion sustaining Orofer despite LOE.
scores.quote: Currently, we are in the investment mode... in pharma, the gestation period is 18 - 24 months but at the same time, the beauty is we are getting prescriptions

scores.rationale: R&D at 4.2% of sales (INR383.5cr, +50bps) has repeatedly converted into commercialized differentiated products — chirality, Orofer FCM, seven marketed biotherapeutics, Amphotericin B launches in Europe, Bevacizumab wet-AMD and Lenacapavir DMF — with a Scientific Advisory Committee shaping ADCs and complex injectables.
scores.quote: we have a strong portfolio of 7 biotherapeutics which we are already marketing, already commercialized and 2 waiting approval

scores.rationale: A consistent record of small complementary bolt-ons (Tillomed, Marcan, Mantra, Manx, Cutimed, Zuventus minority buyout) that visibly drove Europe +29.6% and Canada growth, though the Zuventus integration caused Q4 attrition and domestic growth fell to 5.2%, and net debt rose to INR1,054cr.
scores.quote: Europe is seeing strong traction with very strong growth of 29.6%... realizing the benefit of Amphotericin B and the bolt-on acquisition that we did in the form of Manx

scores.rationale: No discussion of buybacks, dividends or any distribution policy across the calls; capital allocation commentary is confined to debt reduction post-IPO and acquisition pay-outs.

Revenue of INR9,204cr is generated off a capital base carrying INR415cr of D&A, four new plants and INR1,054cr net debt — respectable but not asset-light, and the moat protecting those assets is generic-branded rather than structural.
scores.quote: Depreciation and amortization expense increased to 94 crores from 67 crores year-on-year due to the Mantra acquisition and operationalization of 4 new plants

scores.rationale: Ranked only 12th in India (long runway) yet repeatedly delivered above-industry domestic growth (15.4% in Q3 FY26, 10% FY26) while Canada growth was explicitly attributed to share gains in every call.

scores.rationale: Multi-year executed expansion — Europe scaled 10x in a decade to INR1,850cr (+25.5%), Canada a top-10 generic player at INR1,487cr (+18.7%), emerging markets +21.8% — all delivered rather than promised.
scores.quote: we acquired Tillomed in 2014 and used that as a base to expand Europe-wide in other countries and have scaled up 10x over a period of last 10 years

scores.rationale: India growth splits roughly evenly between 4% volume and 4% price with 1-2% new launches, and mix has been actively dilutive — gross margin fell to 59.3-59.4% on the lower-margin Sanofi OAD in-licensing and faster international growth.
scores.quote: volume would have been about 4% price about 4% and about a 1% to 2% of new launches

scores.rationale: End markets are secularly expanding: India's 1.4bn unmet-need market, the GLP-1/obesity category with 230 comorbidities, a INR14,000cr derma market, and a government INR10,000cr Bio-Pharma SHAKTI push behind biologics.
scores.quote: Emcure remains an India focused company with huge opportunity to tap the unmet medical needs of over 1.4 billion people

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (net debt INR1,054cr against INR1,789cr EBITDA, gross debt cut from INR2,000cr at IPO), the volatile capital-hungry US business was deliberately ring-fenced out, and all deals are bolt-ons rather than transformational.
scores.quote: We have ring fenced the Emcure business from the volatility of the U.S. business

scores.rationale: A stated 5-year roadmap has been repeated and then delivered against in year one — FY26 revenue +16.6% crossing $1bn 'exceeding the guidance', margins +80bps versus the 75-100bps commitment — by a founder with 30 years in the same business.
scores.quote: surpassing $1 billion in revenue and achieving a growth of 16.6% year-on-year, exceeding the guidance that we had given to you

scores.rationale: Management commentary is markedly promotional — repeated self-quotation, aspirational 'most admired company' framing and 'watch this space' teasers — and the board includes a high-profile media-celebrity MD.
scores.quote: watch this space as more exciting opportunities unfold, helping make your company one of the most admired companies within the pharmaceutical industry

scores.rationale: Heavy investment in people is stated and productivity per MR rose from INR5.4 lakh to INR7 lakh, but the leadership pipeline is filled externally (R.S. Vasan from Sun Pharma, new Zuventus team) and attrition runs 20-30% with a Q4 spike that dented domestic growth.
scores.quote: field productivity... has gone up from INR5.4 lakhs per medical representative to INR7 lakhs over a period of last two years

scores.rationale: Management quantifies its own drags and owns the misses — the exact FCM drag, continuing institutional pricing losses, gross-margin dilution from in-licensing, and the self-inflicted Zuventus restructuring that cut Q4 India growth to 5.2% — though it declines to break out Sanofi revenue.
scores.quote: Q4 is when we did the restructuring of the whole team and portfolio. So, most of the slower growth that you are seeing is because of that

scores.rationale: Headline growth is materially flattered by inorganic and non-operational factors — in-licensing (~6-7% of revenue), Manx/Mantra/Zuventus acquisitions and 7-8% currency tailwind in international — leaving base organic growth nearer 9-10%, so the strong optics overstate underlying skill.
scores.quote: Overall, for the international market, the currency impact was about 7% to 8%

scores.rationale: Genuine mind-share positions exist in specific niches — a global patent on Tenecteplase for stroke, market-creating leadership in iron/anemia, and now sole innovator partnership for rDNA semaglutide — but they are niches within a competitive generics business.
scores.quote: We market Tenecteplase for acute ischemic stroke where we hold the global patent for the indication

scores.rationale: Switching costs are weak: once FCM lost patent protection the institutional business was taken on price, and the semaglutide franchise faces immediate generic substitution requiring price flexibility.
scores.quote: where we are seeing still a bit more challenging is on the institution side, where some of the competition is still there at lower pricing

scores.rationale: The markets are fragmented and contested rather than oligopolistic — Emcure is only the 12th largest in India, eight or nine companies bid for the Novo tie-up, and management itself expects fierce competition.
scores.quote: there were at least 8 or 9 companies who were interested in partnering with Novo Nordisk

scores.rationale: Entry barriers collapse at patent expiry and pricing is not rational — FCM institutional business was lost to lower-priced entrants and the flagship semaglutide launch already required an April 2026 price cut.
scores.quote: The initial uptake has been promising, especially after the price cut in April 2026

scores.rationale: Emcure is a structural beneficiary of MNCs exiting Indian promotion — taking over Sanofi's cardiac then oral-antidiabetic portfolios and Roche nephrology — while gaining share from weaker generic players in Canada.
scores.quote: We recently took over the entire Sanofi cardiac portfolio to promote and distribute

scores.rationale: The company is the opposite of under-the-radar — a high-profile 2024 IPO, $1bn revenue, marquee alliances with Novo Nordisk, Sanofi and Roche, and covered by JM, Kotak, Motilal Oswal and ASK on every call.
scores.quote: I would like to thank all the investors, stakeholders and partners who helped us achieve a very successful listing

scores.rationale: Gross margins around 60% and a doctor-facing brand associated with innovation and quality support some pricing power, but margins have drifted down on mix and the promoted-versus-institutional split shows the image premium does not extend everywhere.
scores.quote: Emcure is synonymous in the doctor's chamber with innovation and quality

scores.rationale: The commercial pitch is explicitly reliability-led — quality and scientific data used to defend FCM against cheaper competition, and rDNA-biologic origin plus innovator data used to differentiate Poviztra from synthetic generics.
scores.quote: we are essentially focusing on quality and certain parameters where we are better than the competitors

scores.rationale: A 5,000+ strong field force with 70% specialist prescriptions, deliberate Tier-2/3/4 penetration and pan-India availability gives real customer intimacy, and MNC partners chose Emcure precisely for that reach.
scores.quote: we have recently added 1,200 sales people in the last 18 months, taking our field strength to over 5,000

scores.rationale: The retail/prescriber side is well matched with specialist-led branded intangibles, but roughly half of emerging-markets revenue is price-tendered ARV and Indian institutional sales where trust does not lock in the customer.
scores.quote: ARV would have been roughly about half of it

scores.rationale: A genuine dual capability in chemistry and biologics — chirality, seven marketed biotherapeutics, complex injectables like Amphotericin B, ADCs in development — but 4.2% R&D intensity is solid rather than deep, and the newest growth driver is licensed innovation, not owned.
scores.quote: we are strong in both chemistry and biotech, one of the very few companies in the country which has presence in both biology and chemistry

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the calls; the business model is manufacturing plus prescription detailing.

Commercial reach is the demonstrated moat — three global innovators (Novo Nordisk chosen over 8-9 bidders, Sanofi twice, Roche) selected Emcure to carry their brands in India, alongside a top-10 Canadian generic front-end and Europe-wide presence.
scores.quote: These alliances with leading pharmaceutical companies demonstrate our strong commercial capabilities and scale in the India market

scores.rationale: Growth capex is genuinely high (≈100 new stores in two years, 223 total, plus owned NCR properties), but incremental ROIC has deteriorated sharply — annualized ROCE fell from 28.6% in Q1FY25 to 11% in 9MFY26 as new stores earn 3% EBITDA vs 7.3% for mature ones.
scores.quote: Over the last 2 years, we have added nearly 100 stores, which now account for approximately 50% of our total store portfolio

scores.rationale: A&P is spent reactively on new-market launches and is repeatedly cited as a margin drag rather than as durable brand equity, with no evidence of A&P-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: we have invested in advertising and marketing activities, which has marginally impacted our profitability for the quarter

scores.rationale: No R&D activity or spend is discussed in any call — it is a consumer-durables retailer, not a developer.
No acquisitions are mentioned across the 15 calls; expansion is entirely greenfield store openings.
Asked directly how record FY26 operating cash flow would be deployed, management described only reinvestment and routine loan servicing, articulating no buyback or dividend policy.
scores.quote: the cash flows have all been deployed into other business and whereas the working capital requirement has definitely gone down

scores.rationale: Turnover is reasonable for retail (INR7,183 crores revenue, working capital ~60 days) but the model is not asset-light — owned NCR property, 73 inventory days and Ind AS 116 leases — and returns have fallen to 11% ROCE with no protecting moat.
scores.quote: inventory days outstanding as of 31st March'26 stood at 73 days

scores.rationale: As the #4 national player with a regional base, there is long runway and repeated evidence of share capture in AP/Telangana upcountry and NCR (30% cluster growth) even against new entrants.
scores.quote: We've definitely gained our market share in AP as a cluster, Telangana, UP country market, where the competition is very stiff

scores.rationale: NCR entry was executed and scaled to 30% growth and full-year EBITDA positive, but economics badly lagged the promise — Aug 2024 guided stabilization 'by 26', yet FY26 NCR margin was only ~0.5%, below the 2.6% reported in Q1FY25.
scores.quote: our NCR operations remained EBITDA positive on a nine-month basis, delivering an EBITDA margin of around 0.5%

scores.rationale: Management explicitly describes growth as volume-led with flat realizations, and later upside came from a GST rate cut (a price reduction) rather than own pricing power.
scores.quote: You will not see an absolute value growth coming in. The quantity has increased mainly. So you will see more of volume growth compared to a value growth

scores.rationale: FY26 is clearly a cycle trough with an identifiable upturn — weak prior summer creating a low cooling-product base, GST cut, income-tax relief and an AI-phone replacement cycle, with Q4FY26 SSSG already rebounding to 12.2%.
scores.quote: the AC base being -- or the cooling product base being quite low in the last quarter... I think the coming summer quarters are going to be good

scores.rationale: The Indian consumer-durables end market is structurally under-penetrated with rising disposable income, and management points to multiple unpenetrated categories plus new ones (dishwashers, built-ins, induction).
scores.quote: Several categories in our portfolio continue to remain unpenetrated, offering significant growth potential

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic with no M&A, leverage is prudent (net debt/equity 0.2x, net debt/EBITDA 0.36x) and management stayed selective on new geographies while prioritizing working-capital discipline.
scores.quote: The gross debt and net debt to equity stood at INR0.2X and our net debt to EBITDA stood at INR0.36X

scores.rationale: The promoter-CEO has stuck to the same cluster-deepening strategy since 2022 and persisted with a loss-making NCR cluster for four years until it turned full-year EBITDA positive.
scores.quote: Our strategy remains centred on solidifying our presence in existing markets before venturing into new territories

scores.rationale: Calls are run by just the promoter-CEO and CFO with plain operational detail and no celebrity positioning or grand vision statements across all 15 calls.
scores.quote: MANAGEMENT : MR. KARAN BAJAJ – CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER AND PROMOTER... MR. PREMCHAND DEVARAKONDA – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or internal leadership pipeline appears in any excerpt.

Disclosure improved over time to mature-vs-new store revenue and margin splits and cluster-level profitability, and weak numbers are acknowledged rather than spun, though one analyst's presentation discrepancy was deferred offline.
scores.quote: the mature stores continue to demonstrate strong performance with an EBITDA margin of 7%, whereas the new stores are currently operating an EBITDA margin of 3%

scores.rationale: Headline growth is largely explained by store additions and external tailwinds (GST cut, heat wave, festive timing) rather than operating skill — 9MFY26 SSSG was 0.19% and ROCE fell to 11%, so the reported growth overstates underlying capability.
scores.quote: For 9MFY '26, SSSG stood at 0.19%. ROCE and ROE on an annualized basis for 9MFY '26 stood at 11% and 5.8%

scores.rationale: The Bajaj Electronics brand holds a near mind-space monopoly in its core Hyderabad cluster with very high market share built over decades, though this does not extend outside the South.

scores.rationale: Barriers are low — new players entered the South cluster during the period and management admits competition compressed gross margins in Telangana/AP.
scores.quote: Telangana, UP country market, where the competition is very stiff

scores.rationale: The cluster-based model delivers dense local accessibility (223 stores, 66+ cities, one-stop 6,000+ SKU format) reinforced by embedded NBFC/EMI financing at the point of sale.

scores.rationale: The customer is retail, but the benefits offered are convenience and finance rather than the intangible/brand pull the framework prefers for retail buyers, so the match is only partial.

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology or tech-led differentiation is claimed anywhere in the calls.

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

R&D exists (process R&D team with PhDs, early TOPCon adoption, G12R transition) but management could not quantify spend or five-year growth when directly asked, and the technology is largely equipment-embedded rather than proprietary.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed across any call; growth is entirely greenfield/organic, so there is no M&A track record to judge.

scores.rationale: End market is in genuine secular expansion — ~60GW annualised Indian solar installations plus storage, green hydrogen, EVs and data-centre demand, with government renewable targets reaffirmed.
scores.quote: electric mobility, energy storage, green hydrogen, and data centers are creating a significant long-term opportunity

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, INR1,621 crore of debt prepaid from IPO proceeds taking net debt/equity to negative, two rating upgrades in a year, and backward integration deliberately timed rather than rushed.
scores.quote: As of March 31, 2026, our net debt to equity stood at negative 0.06x

scores.rationale: Three-decade evolution from solar water heaters to integrated PV, with self-directed timing on technology (early TOPCon) and market pivots (Europe to US to India), though the listed track record is only three quarters long.

scores.quote: we have experienced a remarkable transition from a closely held organization to a publicly listed enterprise

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession planning or leadership pipeline in any of the four calls beyond generic thanks to employees.

Generally forthcoming — detailed, specific answers on inventory build, inter-company eliminations, advance reversals and export competitiveness — but deflected the R&D spend question and has not yet had to own a miss.
scores.quote: So, to be very candid, I mean, other than China, yes, all other regions is something that India can compete with

scores.quote: To give you a perspective of how fragmented the industry is

scores.rationale: No two-sided network or platform dynamic exists or is discussed anywhere in the calls.

scores.rationale: Calls are uniformly operational and factual — plant-by-plant SOP dates and order values — with no personality-driven narrative or promotional framing.

scores.quote: This merger will create a $1 billion revenue packaging powerhouse... Post -merger, IVL will hold 51.8% of MergeCo and will be promoter of EPL

scores.rationale: Dividend was withheld in FY26 (for a defensible merger-mechanics reason), no buyback discipline is evidenced, and capital allocation is deferred to the Board with cash earmarked as an M&A 'war chest'.
scores.quote: I noticed no dividend this time... the dividend is actually because of the merger

scores.rationale: This is an asset-heavy converter — 21 plants in 11 countries, greenfields in Brazil/Thailand and capex above depreciation — with ROCE only reaching 19% after 15 quarters of improvement.
scores.quote: We operate across 21 manufacturing sites in 11 countries

scores.rationale: Repeated, multi-year evidence of wallet-share capture off a ~35% base via sustainability leadership, plus a large runway in Beauty & Cosmetics where it grew 30% and is now bigger than Oral Care in most key markets.
scores.quote: we have gained wallet with two more customers in Europe, which we never used to do earlier

scores.rationale: Brazil moved from announcement (2022) to commercialisation to multi-customer outperformance, Thailand was entered in nine months, and the Indovida merger opens Southeast Asia and Africa — a promise-to-delivery record across the period.
scores.quote: EPL was able to enter the market in less than 9 months, our shortest time of entry in any new markets

scores.rationale: Pricing is largely cost pass-through (with negative price corrections in FY25 when commodities softened) so growth is volume- and mix-led rather than priced; the B&C mix shift is favourable but has yielded only ~50bps annual margin expansion.
scores.quote: Globally, there is no material negative pricing... Maybe no major positive prices either, because that's how commodities are moving

scores.rationale: The visible cycle is input costs, and the company sits at the start of a fresh inflation shock rather than near a trough, partly offset by a stated Oral Care recovery from prior-year headwinds.
scores.quote: The crisis has affected both the availability and cost of our key raw materials

scores.rationale: Two durable tailwinds are evidenced — mandated conversion to sustainable/laminated tubes (including aluminium-to-laminate in pharma) and emerging-market consumption at 75% of combined revenue — though the underlying tube market itself grows only modestly.
scores.quote: we are taking the lead on sustainability and this has helped us to get wallet share gain with a few key customers

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (net debt/EBITDA 0.52x falling to 0.25x) and investment is counter-cyclical/ahead of the curve, but the strategy explicitly embraces large inorganic moves culminating in a company-doubling merger.
scores.quote: inorganic opportunities will remain an important part of our strategy

scores.rationale: The 20%+ EBITDA margin and sustained double-digit growth targets set in 2022 were pursued relentlessly and delivered by FY26, with 500bps of margin gain over 15 quarters, though the company operates under successive PE/strategic promoters.
scores.quote: we have delivered 500 basis points of EBITDA margin improvement over the last 15 quarters

scores.rationale: The business is an unglamorous B2B converter and calls are largely operational, but management leans on awards, ratings and superlative framing around the merger.
scores.quote: what we believe is one of the most exciting and transformational chapters in our company's journey

scores.rationale: There is systematic capability investment and Great Place to Work certification in seven countries, but the internal pipeline looks thin given repeated CFO/Chairman churn and an externally recruited CEO succession.
scores.quote: EPL was certified as a Great Place to Work across seven countries this year

scores.rationale: Management consistently names its own shortfalls without prompting — calling Europe margins 'not acceptable' in 2022 and admitting the India B&C miss in 2024 — and refuses to give timing commitments it cannot back.
scores.quote: B&C in AMESA, particularly in India, could have been better, maybe should have been better

scores.rationale: The improvement looks skill-driven rather than lucky — margins rose region by region (Europe +230bps, Americas from single-digits to high-teens) against, not with, the commodity cycle — but ROCE of 19% and an untested doubling merger temper the conclusion.
scores.quote: In Europe, margins have increased by 230 basis points over the past year... in the Americas, margins have risen from single -digits to high -teens

scores.rationale: EPL holds a leading ~35% share of a global oral-care tube market with only four players and is the sole India-based packaging company with EcoVadis Platinum, but its customers are giant FMCG buyers.
scores.quote: oral care is a very concentrated marketplace, right, there are only four players in the world

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real — long-term oral care commitments, B2B vendor onboarding approvals, and plants sited next to anchor customers — which is why gained wallet share is described as sticky.
scores.quote: any oral care commitment, as you know, are long -term commitments... these are all wallet share gains, it will remain with us

scores.rationale: The structure is a genuine four-player global oligopoly, but the end customers are Colgate/Unilever-scale buyers who extract price corrections when commodities fall, capping the benefit.
scores.quote: have there been some price corrections in a few places with a few customers based on... commodity softening of the past... Yes, there has been

scores.rationale: No new entrants appear across five years of calls, pricing behaviour is contractual pass-through rather than discounting, and sustainability certification plus capital intensity raise the bar — though ownership has shifted from Blackstone toward Indorama.
scores.quote: With nearly 50% of our business covered under contractual pass -through arrangements

scores.rationale: Weaker aluminium-tube converters in pharma and smaller rivals unable to secure raw material in the current crisis are explicit sources of share for EPL.
scores.quote: there would be some opportunity for market share gains as well

scores.rationale: Tube converting is an unglamorous niche, but EPL is a widely covered listed company with global PE/strategic sponsors and is now building a $1bn platform — no longer capital-ignored.
scores.quote: creating a consumer packaging leader focused on emerging markets

scores.rationale: As a B2B supplier EPL has no image- or taste-driven pricing power; realised price moves with polymer and energy costs and gross margin is defended through pass-throughs, not brand.
scores.quote: our model is a landed cost plus power pass -through model

scores.rationale: Customers demonstrably buy certainty — supply security in the Middle East crisis, decades-long supplier partnerships, and ESG-compliance assurance that won wallet share ahead of price.
scores.quote: We are prioritizing supply security for our customers... strength of our decades -long supplier partnerships and meaningful scale allow us to be a reliable partner

scores.rationale: EPL builds capacity physically next to customers and has invested in front-end 'hunting' and specialised sales capability to deepen customer intimacy.
scores.quote: We have finalized the location of the factory which is close to one of our key customers

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate and the benefit set is correctly matched — reliability, pass-through economics, qualification/switching-cost lock-in — rather than misplaced consumer-style intangibles.
scores.quote: In B2B businesses most times the vendor onboarding approvals are required

scores.rationale: A real multi-product technical edge in sustainable and extruded tube formats (Platina, Neo-seam, first Indian packaging MNC with SBTi approval) that customers pay for in share, though R&D intensity is not disclosed as high.
scores.quote: we secured approval for our emission targets from the Science Based Targets initiative, or SBTi, becoming the first Indian MNC in the packaging sector

scores.rationale: Nothing in five years of calls suggests a two-sided or self-reinforcing network; the model is contract manufacturing of tubes for individual FMCG customers.

A 21-plant, 11-country footprint lets EPL follow global customers anywhere and secure supply when rivals cannot, a reach smaller regional converters cannot match, though it required heavy capital rather than being self-funding.
scores.quote: in our case, we've been able to secure supplies of all our raw materials... we do feel that we have some competitive advantage in a situation like this

scores.rationale: Continuous and rising 'growth' spend on technology (loan origination system, Microsoft Dynamics CRM, apps, credit cards/PL/AD1) is real but incremental returns have been poor — cost-to-income stuck at ~70-72% and ROA only reached 1.46% in Q4 FY26 after years of investment.
scores.quote: as we continue to invest in our various product technology initiative, our cost to income will remain at more or less similar levels of last year

scores.rationale: Marketing is described as high-visibility social-media campaigns around a 'beyond banking' theme, but there is no evidence it built pricing power — deposits are still won by raising rates.
scores.quote: backed by predominantly marketing campaign, high visibility, high penetration, high impact which we do it through predominantly on social media platform

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or R&D-efficiency discussion in any call; technology spend is discussed as opex/infrastructure, not R&D.

The only corporate action is the regulatory reverse merger of the holding company (executed ahead of schedule) plus a INR1,343 crore direct-assignment Agri pool purchase — neither is a strategic bolt-on that improved operating margin.
scores.quote: we have progress well on our reverse merger... we will probably do that a few months ahead of that schedule

scores.rationale: No dividend or buyback policy is discussed across the 16 calls; capital talk is entirely about conservation and possible future raises.

As a balance-sheet lender it is structurally asset-heavy and low-return — ROA moved from ~0.65% to 1.46% only at the best quarter, with NIM compressing from ~8.5-9% to 7.29% as the high-yield MFI mix fell.
scores.quote: pre-crisis, our NIM used to be anywhere between 8.5% to 9%... somewhere around 7% to 7.1% is where we believe it should kind of stabilize

scores.rationale: Small base with long runway and demonstrated share capture on the asset side — advances +22% YoY with record disbursements in FY26, though deposit growth lagged at 8%.
scores.quote: Gross advances grew 22% year-on-year to INR46,165 crores, driven by robust disbursement

scores.rationale: Expansion is incremental within India (housing live in TN, AP, Telangana, Karnataka) plus an NR deposit franchise across 140+ countries — credible but not a premium brand travelling into new markets.
scores.quote: NR now we have crossed INR2,000 crores, and we are almost presented in 140-plus countries

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/disbursement-led while both pricing and mix worked against them — yield on advances fell and mix shifted away from high-yield microfinance.
scores.quote: the yield on gross advances declined by 10 bps quarter-on-quarter to 15.63%, primarily due to the lower contribution from the MFI mix

scores.rationale: The bank is visibly coming off the bottom of the microfinance credit cycle, with credit cost falling from 2.74% to 1.11%, net slippage at a 10-quarter low and NIM inflecting up for the first time in years.
scores.quote: The NIM increased for the first time in the -- in Q3 after many years of decline... credit cost at 1.11% for the Q4 came in lowest compared to the previous 8 quarters

scores.rationale: End market is lending to India's informal and formalizing economy — a secularly expanding pool, with all product lines (housing, MSE, used vehicles) growing 20%+ and guidance of 20%+ advances growth.
scores.quote: we are using to lend to the borrowers in the informal and formalizing economy through a very well diversified loan platform

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, no acquisitions, deliberate de-risking by cutting microfinance from ~20% to ~10% of book, proactive PCR build to 70%+ and capital-conservation via IBPC/CGTMSE.
scores.quote: During Q3, we took some initiatives to conserve capital, such as increasing the IBPC outstanding from INR1,250 crores to INR2,000 crores

scores.rationale: Vasudevan has led across all 16 calls with a consistently articulated multi-year build-out thesis, and stuck to it through the restructuring pool, the MFI crisis and NIM compression.
scores.quote: We are about 8 years in. We've got another 3 to 4 years left for us to emerge as a bank where most of the investments would have happened

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently operational and detail-driven with a broad management bench presenting, no promotional framing or celebrity-CEO posture.
