scores.quote: approval of financial statements, final dividend for FY2022

scores.rationale: Life insurance is structurally capital- and balance-sheet-heavy — ₹3.34 trillion AUM against a 225% solvency requirement — and returns are modest, with RoEV of 11.9% in FY2026, the opposite of an asset-light compounder.
scores.quote: Consequently, the RoEV for FY2026 stands at 11.9%.

scores.rationale: Share gains are episodic rather than sustained: new business sum assured share peaked at 15.8% in Q1-FY2023 and had fallen to 11.8% by Q1-FY2027, even as retail protection grew 60%+ post-GST reform.
scores.quote: Our sum assured market share stood at 11.8%.

scores.rationale: Expansion is entirely domestic micro-market and branch densification, with the only overseas angle being the NRI segment via GIFT City — credible but small and unquantified.
scores.quote: focus will be to deepen NRI segment through GIFT city

scores.rationale: Recent value growth is explicitly mix-led — protection mix up 220bps, longer policy tenor (26 to 29 years), higher sum assured multiples and rider attachment driving margin from 22.8% to 24.7% to 26.7% — though the company disclaims pricing power in non-par.
scores.quote: we have also been working towards improving the profitability of each line of business through longer tenor policies, higher sum assured multiples and increasing rider attachment

scores.rationale: The savings/non-par cycle appears near a trough with an identifiable catalyst — management expects a pickup as competing fixed-income 'sticker prices' temper — while protection is already in an upcycle from GST exemption.
scores.quote: As time goes by and we see some sort of tempering of those alternative investments, we should start to see some pickup on the non-par side as well.

scores.rationale: Indian retail protection is a genuinely under-penetrated secular market, repeatedly quantified by management at only ~13% of the addressable population covered, with 5- and 10-year new business sum assured CAGRs of 18.7% and 25.1%.
scores.quote: With only about 13% of the addressable population currently covered through retail protection, we believe this segment presents a significant long-term growth opportunity spanning multiple decades.

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, no acquisitions, solvency consistently 185-227% versus a 150% requirement, zero NPAs since inception, and explicit willingness to forgo group term volumes that fail risk-reward tests.
scores.quote: we continue to maintain our track record of not having a single non-performing asset in our investment portfolio since inception

scores.rationale: The team has stuck to an absolute-VNB objective and multi-year agency rebuild through two CEO transitions and adverse regulation, explicitly refusing to manage to a margin number, though the agency investment has yet to show returns (2% growth in Q1-FY2027).
scores.quote: We don't have a margin fixation... Absolute VNB is what we look at growing.

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently delivered by a functional bench (CFO, CIO, Appointed Actuary, HR head) with substance-heavy disclosure and no promotional or personality-driven commentary, and no forward guidance is offered.
scores.quote: Dhiren Salian: No, no guidance.

scores.rationale: Evident internal pipeline — Amish Banker rose from branch operations to COO to Chief Distribution Officer succeeding a two-decade veteran, and CFO succession (Jambunathan to Salian) was also internal — plus systematic advisor capability building.
scores.quote: Amish started his career in branch operations and has a deep understanding of the customer life cycle... will be taking over as Chief Distribution Officer from Amit Palta.

scores.rationale: Management proactively disclosed and explained the ₹2.64bn negative persistency variance on its own flagship annuity product and the input-tax-credit drag, though it declined to quantify the GST margin impact when pressed.
scores.quote: Persistency variance is a negative ■ 2.64 billion, which is largely on account of the 100% premium back annuity product where the persistency experience fell short of long-term assumptions.

scores.rationale: Headline VNB and protection growth are substantially externally driven — GST exemption on protection lifted industry retail sum assured 2.5x — and stripping that out leaves FY2026 APE growth of just 2.2%, so results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: The retail sum assured growth for the industry was higher by 2.5 times in the post reform period as compared to the pre-reform period.

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold anywhere in the value chain; even in group term, where the company claims the largest share, 12-15% of customers defect to competitors every single year at renewal.
scores.quote: incidentally 12% to 15% of the business that doesn't get renewed and gets renewed with any other competition insurer

scores.rationale: Some lock-in exists via long-tenor policies and 84% 13th-month persistency, but the 2024 surrender-value regulations and observed early withdrawals show switching costs are being actively legislated down.
scores.quote: customers used the amount for withdrawals in times of need

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented and price-competitive rather than a stable oligopoly, with management describing 'very, very competitive practices' in group term and price-driven customer defection to fixed deposits in savings.
scores.quote: the growth has been relatively subdued because of very, very competitive practices

scores.rationale: Regulatory capital and solvency rules create real entry barriers and ownership is stable (ICICI Bank promoter), but pricing rationality is poor — competitors' 'sticker price' wars in non-par and group term compress economics.
scores.quote: there are products on the fixed income side that at this point are little more lucrative for the customer when compared to some of our products, purely from a sticker price perspective

scores.rationale: Weaker players clearly exist and the company took share in credit life 'almost twice the rate of credit growth', but it has also been a donator itself, ceding new business sum assured share from 15.8% to 11.8%.
scores.quote: this business has been almost growing twice the rate of credit growth in the banking setup

scores.rationale: This is a large listed insurer with a quarterly analyst call attended by Nomura, Ambit, B&K, Bernstein and 360 One — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Our next question comes from the line of Manas Agrawal with Sanford C. Bernstein.

scores.rationale: Demand is demonstrably price-elastic rather than image-driven — customers rotate to fixed deposits on headline yield — and the company's own name change to leverage the ICICI brand implicitly concedes the insurance brand alone is not the pull.
scores.quote: Largely fixed deposits. The sticker price, yes, the sticker price of some of these products is extremely high. So that does tend to attract customers

scores.rationale: The core product sold is certainty, and delivery is best-in-class and consistent: 99.3% claim settlement ratio, 1-day average turnaround, 22% early claims ratio described as best in industry, and no NPA in the portfolio since inception.
scores.quote: we maintained an industry-leading claim settlement ratio of 99.3% with an average turnaround time of 1.1 days

scores.rationale: Access is exceptionally broad and getting broader — 2.44 lakh advisors, 52 bank tie-ups spanning 26,800 branches and 1,500+ non-bank partners — combined with process intimacy such as same-day issuance and same-day commission payouts.
scores.quote: we are also the first life insurer to pay out commissions on the same day to our distributors

scores.rationale: The benefit type is reasonably matched to customer — reliability and claims certainty for retail, and disciplined risk-reward underwriting plus TCO negotiation for corporate group term — though corporate lock-in is weak given annual repricing.
scores.quote: We understand this segment well and will underwrite business only if it matches our risk reward expectations.

scores.rationale: AI/ML is embedded end-to-end with measurable outcomes — 71% reduction in fraud-prone cases, 85% digital KYC, 48% same-day issuance, 40-50bps annual savings cost reduction — but these are process efficiencies replicable by peers, not a multi-product proprietary edge.
scores.quote: Our focus on data analytics to mitigate insurance risk at onboarding stage has led to 71% reduction in cases with higher propensity for fraud and early claims for savings policies.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is self-reinforcing two-sided; distribution scale is bought through commissions and partner additions, and partner banks can and do recalibrate volumes away from the company.
scores.quote: The growth reflects the continued recalibration of business at some of our partner banks

scores.rationale: Genuinely deep multi-channel reach — bancassurance across 52 banks/26,800 branches, 2.44 lakh advisors, 1,500+ partnerships and 47 new partners added in a single quarter — but comparable networks exist at SBI Life and HDFC Life, and proprietary channels have recently stalled at ~2% growth.
scores.quote: we have the strength of 2.44 lakh plus advisors, 52 bank partnerships with access to more than 26,800 bank branches and 1,500+ non-bank partnerships

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex across the period — 25,000 spindles/Rs.270cr in FY23, 153mn meter capacity build-out, a greenfield North Carolina pillow plant lifting capacity from 13mn to 31mn pillows, and a fresh Rs.250cr outlay — but incremental ROIC is currently poor (EBITDA margin fell to 11% in FY26 from 13.8%, PAT halved) with returns still promised rather than delivered.
scores.quote: we have largely completed our planned growth investments, positioning the company to benefit from significant operating leverage opportunities going forward

scores.rationale: A&P spend on Wamsutta/Fieldcrest/Waverly branding has been deliberate and rising since FY25, with early evidence of traction (new business at INR792cr, strong product reviews), but it has cost 150-200bps of EBITDA for two years and durable brand equity/pricing power is not yet proven.
scores.quote: EBITDA was impacted due to conscious increase in branding expenses along with investment in human resources to support the new acquisition and licensing business

scores.rationale: No discussion of R&D spend or R&D-driven product pipelines in the excerpts; product development is described as sourcing-led and design/licensing-led rather than R&D.

M&A has been frequent and mixed — the large GHCL home textiles acquisition (45mn meters capacity, only 20mn utilised) still sat under-sweated years later, while the small, cash-funded Wamsutta brand buy (INR85cr from internal accruals) is complementary and performing, but post-deal OPM has fallen not improved.
scores.quote: The successful acquisition of Wamsutta, the U.S. national brand, through internal accruals of INR85 crores, reinforces our global home textile vision.

scores.rationale: Only a modest final dividend of INR1.50 per INR2 face-value share is evident, with no buyback programme or articulated distribution policy — cash is being directed to capex and debt reduction instead.
scores.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share for the face value of INR2 each

scores.rationale: This is a capital-heavy spinning/weaving/processing business with 121-132 working capital days, INR760cr net debt and repeated large capex, and the acquired capacity ran at ~65-70% utilisation for years — the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: our existing 2 U.S. utility bedding manufacturing facilities are currently operating at around 65% utilization

scores.rationale: Consistent evidence of share capture — India's bed linen import share in the US rising, six consecutive TEXPROCIL gold trophies, no customer loss through the tariff shock, and deliberate margin sacrifice to hold share — though it is already the largest global bed linen player, limiting runway in its core.
scores.quote: In order to sustain volumes and protect our market share, we undertook calibrated product mix adjustments and shared a part of the tariff burden to support our customers.

scores.rationale: Geographic diversification has been a stated priority for years and is now delivering — non-US at ~30% of core revenue, presence in 50+ countries, three US manufacturing facilities built, and EU/UK FTA optionality — but the promised US brand and European scale-up is still largely ahead rather than banked.
scores.quote: Today, non-U.S. markets contribute to approximately 30% of our core business revenue.

scores.rationale: Growth has been volume- and capacity-led rather than price-led, and the company demonstrably lacks pricing power — it absorbed tariff and Russia-oil penalty costs via discounts, saw volumes fall from 106.4mn to 94.1mn meters, and EBITDA margin compress from 13.8% to 11%.
scores.quote: a part of the tariff impact and the Russia oil -related penalty impact was absorbed to protect customer relationships and preserve market share

scores.rationale: The company is visibly at a cyclical trough with an identifiable upturn — FY26 margins bottomed at 11% under a 50% tariff, and the US trade deal plus EU FTA have now removed the overhang, underpinning guidance for 30%+ revenue growth and a record FY27.
scores.quote: we are on track to deliver a record year in FY27. We expect volumes to be in the range of 105 million to 110 million meters compared to 94 million meters achieved in FY26

scores.rationale: The China+1 sourcing shift, a string of FTAs (Australia, UAE, Japan, EU, US) and a USD30bn EU plus large US home textile market give a credible multi-year structural tailwind, though home textiles itself is a mature, GDP-linked consumer category rather than a secular growth market.
scores.quote: With the EU FTA, textile exports from India to Europe will now become duty-free. This is a significant structural advantage as it creates a level playing field for the Indian players.

scores.rationale: Leverage is managed prudently (net debt cut INR215cr, capex 75% internal accruals, debt-free phase in FY25) and investment continued counter-cyclically through the tariff shock, but the record includes a large transformative GHCL acquisition and serial brand/licensing deals rather than a purely organic focus.
scores.quote: We have announced a capex of INR250 crores, which will be funded by internal accruals, 75% and 25% by debt.

scores.rationale: Management has held to a consistent multi-year vision — value-added/branded shift articulated from 2022, the doubling-revenue-by-2028 goal reaffirmed through the tariff crisis, and greenfield US manufacturing built while the environment was hostile.
scores.quote: we stay committed to our long -term vision of doubling our revenues by 2028, supported by a well -balanced mix of business and geographies

scores.rationale: Calls are workmanlike and operations-focused with no personality promotion, though there is heavy self-promotion of awards and ESG scores in every prepared remark.
scores.quote: This award is a strong validation of our consistent export performance, our leadership position in the category

scores.rationale: Talent investment is visible — hiring US brand teams ahead of revenue and a smooth CEO-to-Executive Vice Chairman leadership transition between FY25 and FY26 calls — but there is no described systematic talent development or succession programme.
scores.quote: In Indo Count Global, our U.S. entity, we have appointed new talent in order to manage the brand and promote it.

scores.rationale: Management quantifies bad news specifically (INR9.2cr labour code hit, 150-200bps incubation drag, low-teen core decline, 100bps tariff hit) and admits uncertainty rather than bluffing, though it also deflects sharply on hard questions.
scores.quote: our core business witnessed a low -teen decline during the year

scores.rationale: Much of the favourable narrative rests on external factors — FTAs, China+1, favourable exchange rate, tariff normalisation — rather than demonstrated skill, and the actual delivered record shows repeated guidance slippage (FY26 EBITDA 11% vs a long-guided 16-18% band, brand payoff pushed from FY26 to FY27+).
scores.quote: EBITDA grew 22% on Y -o-Y basis due to normalization of down trading scenario, improved realizations in the core business and favourable exchange rate.

scores.rationale: It is the largest global bed linen maker with six consecutive export gold trophies, but that is scale leadership in a contract-manufacturing category serving big-box retailers, not a monopoly in the end customer's mind or a captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: the Gold Trophy for the highest exports of bed sheets in the cotton made -ups category for the sixth consecutive year

scores.rationale: Switching costs are low — the company had to hand customers discounts to keep orders during the tariff period and competes against Pakistan, China and other Indian exporters on a level-playing-field basis once duties equalise.
scores.quote: Yes, we did give a case -to-case basis, tariff discounts to customers

scores.rationale: The customer side is highly concentrated big-box US retailers with strong negotiating power, while the supply side is fragmented across Indian, Chinese and Pakistani exporters — the reverse of a favourable oligopoly.
scores.quote: reflecting a strong trend across big box retaile rs and omni -channel platforms

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and pricing is not rational — capacity is added freely across the industry, tariff costs were passed back as customer discounts, and MMF/polyester entrants and other exporting nations are explicitly identified as competitive threats.
scores.quote: Indian players have lagged a bit in terms of gaining market share on those presence

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are clearly identified and share is available — Pakistan described as economically weak and low-end, and China's dominance of the utility bedding category eroding under China+1.
scores.quote: The China as a country is dominating this category for a long time, and we are seeing some green shoots for Indian companies to strengthen their position in this business.

scores.rationale: Home textile exports is a well-covered, heavily analyst-followed listed sector with FTA-driven attention, and management actively courts visibility through awards, ESG rankings and IR advisors rather than staying under the radar.
scores.quote: we now rank within the top 3 perce ntile globally among textile, apparel and luxury goods industry peers in ESG performance

scores.rationale: The Wamsutta relaunch, licensed brands and 63% gross margin point to intangible-driven ambitions, but demand proved discretionary and price-sensitive (down-trading, discounting, consumers deferring purchases) rather than image-insulated.
scores.quote: consumers are spending on essential products rather than discretionary purchases

scores.rationale: Reliability and supply-chain certainty are the company's genuine selling proposition — it forgoes cost to protect OTIF service levels, retained every customer through the tariff shock, and positions itself as a preferred long-term sourcing partner.
scores.quote: we forgo the cost at the level of providing service to the customer... keeping in mind the customer service and not the cost

scores.rationale: Customer proximity is being built deliberately — three US manufacturing facilities across Midwest, West Coast and East Coast for responsiveness, plus ~2,000 domestic touch points and omnichannel/D2C reach.
scores.quote: It enables customer proximity, improves responsiveness and gives us clear operational flexibility.

scores.rationale: The benefit match is only partly right — it correctly sells reliability and end-to-end range to corporate big-box retailers, but those buyers retain the negotiating power (tariff discounts) and the retail-facing brand strategy is still unproven.
scores.quote: The ability to offer a range of collections across bed, bath, utility bedding, etcetera, strengthens our value proposition and enhances the wallet share with our retail partners.

scores.rationale: No technology edge is evidenced — advantage is described in terms of capacity, cotton availability, service and sustainability certifications, with only generic references to leveraging advanced technologies.
scores.quote: Our strategy involves leveraging advanced technologies, boosting customer engagement through digital platforms

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic in the excerpts.

Distribution reach is a genuine relative strength — largest global bed linen capacity, presence in 50+ countries across 5 continents, three US plants for local fulfilment and 2,000 domestic touch points — though rivals can and do replicate capacity.
scores.quote: With our presence across 50 -plus countries spanning 5 continents, we are positioned to unlock the next phase of global growth

scores.rationale: The only investment discussed is ongoing IT/digital spend with no sizing, no growth-vs-maintenance split and no incremental ROIC evidence; the bank has no DBU rollout yet.
scores.quote: there is good investment in IT expenditure so as to improve further our mobile banking and other areas

scores.rationale: Neither call mentions advertising, promotion or brand spend.
No R&D spend or new-product development pipeline is discussed in either call.
No acquisitions at all — the activity is in the opposite direction, monetising non-core stakes (Ageas Federal life JV, NSE), which is tidy but gives no evidence on bolt-on acquisition skill.
scores.quote: a gain of Rs.380 Crores coming from the sale of our stake in Ageas Federal

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed; the only ownership event mentioned is the government's divestment process run by DIPAM, which is not a distribution.
A structurally asset-heavy, leveraged balance sheet (Rs.3.09 lakh crore assets, leverage ratio 7.5%) earning ~1% ROA, with no moat protecting the spread.
scores.quote: the ROA for the quarter is 1.09 on annualized basis

scores.rationale: 17% advances growth is essentially in line with system credit growth of ~17%, i.e. recovering lost book post-PCA rather than capturing share.
scores.quote: about 17% has been the credit growth in the last month's reporting Friday, and we are also... almost there

scores.rationale: No discussion of new geographies, branch expansion plans or overseas presence in either call.

Earnings growth is led by spread/mix — NIM up 135bps YoY to 4.37% on faster asset repricing and a 56% CASA base — rather than by volume alone, though this is rate-cycle driven not durable pricing power.
scores.quote: NIM at 4.37% has improved by 1.35% year on year

scores.rationale: Classic bottom-of-cycle positioning: just exited PCA, credit cost collapsed to 0.18%, NPAs falling, and management sees the private investment cycle turning with a multi-year credit upturn ahead.
scores.quote: the private sector investment, which was very low in the last 3 years is back on the table... credit growth should be quite robust in the next 2 years

scores.rationale: Indian credit and retail/digital banking is a genuinely secular end market, evidenced by pent-up retail credit demand persisting despite rate hikes, though management's framing is generic macro commentary.
scores.quote: a lot of pent-up demand in consumer financing, home loan financing is showing up, and there is no letup in the demand for retail credit growth

scores.rationale: Consistently conservative: voluntary provisioning far above regulatory requirement (Rs.777cr then ~Rs.1,000cr contingency), 97.86% PCR, 19.5% CRAR, calibrated corporate growth and no acquisitions — though this follows years of capital destruction that required a state bailout.
scores.quote: we have made some proactive and enhanced provisioning, which is not otherwise required by the regulator

scores.rationale: Tenacious execution through the PCA exit and turnaround, but independence is structurally absent — ownership and even the bank's future are decided by DIPAM/LIC, and management repeatedly disclaims any say.
scores.quote: this entire process of disinvestment is being held by DIPAM... they are only running the process

scores.rationale: Calls are low-key and technical with no personality cult, but the bank is a headline privatisation candidate and the MD closes with promotional flourish rather than pure substance.
scores.quote: as we move forward, there will be a lot of pleasant surprises

scores.rationale: No recruitment for roughly four years under PCA and hiring only just restarting, with no evidence of systematic talent development or a leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: we have not done any major recruitment for nearly 4 years mainly because we are under PCA

scores.rationale: Management proactively strips out one-offs and tells analysts not to compare against a flattered base, and reports guidance-versus-actual line by line, though it also leans on 'highest in industry' framing.
scores.quote: since high one-off income was there in June 2021, so the numbers will have to be seen in Q-o-Q reference March 2022

scores.rationale: The record profit is heavily assisted by non-repeatable items — Rs.380cr and Rs.141cr stake-sale gains, interest on income-tax refunds, provision write-backs and rate-cycle NIM — so results overstate underlying operating skill.
scores.quote: If we exclude the gains from strategic sales, the operation profit has shown a growth of 36% year-on-year and a small reduction of 4% from last quarter

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere; the bank is a price-taker on both sides, explicitly declining to lead on deposit pricing and following market rates on loans.
scores.quote: We have increased deposits rates, slightly behind the market mainly because we do not want not play a leader function here

scores.rationale: A 56% CASA ratio implies genuinely sticky, low-cost retail relationships (cost of deposits 3.44%), but there is no regional monopoly or captive aftermarket lock-in.
scores.quote: CASA continues to be high at 56%

scores.rationale: Indian banking is shown as fragmented and competitive, with all banks chasing the same liability relationships and customers free to move on rate.
scores.quote: Banks are increasing deposit rates. There is some chase for liability relationship deposits as well

scores.rationale: Licensing does limit new entrants, but pricing is far from rational — deposit rates are being bid up across the system and IDBI's own ownership is unstable pending privatisation.
scores.quote: We are strategizing to increase the deposit rate to respond to the market moves made by other banks

scores.rationale: IDBI has itself been the share donator — it lost mid-corporate relationships during PCA and is now trying to win them back rather than feeding on weaker rivals.
scores.quote: all the mid corporates that were there in our book earlier but had to exit during PCA regime

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a state-owned bank whose privatisation is a live media and capital-market event with analysts quoting EOI documents on the call.
scores.quote: there was a news that $7.7 billion is expected out of your value

scores.rationale: Low funding cost from a strong CASA base hints at some franchise trust, but banking here is a commodity with no image-driven pricing power and margins driven by the rate cycle.
scores.quote: Cost of deposit stands at 3.44 and cost of funds at 3.72

scores.rationale: Retention of a high CASA base through the crisis suggests residual depositor trust, but the bank's PCA history and NPA record undercut any claim that customers buy IDBI for certainty.
scores.quote: CASA ratio has improved to 55%

scores.rationale: Genuine accessibility across ATM, net and mobile channels with 95% of customer-induced transactions digital, plus financial-inclusion reach, though it has not yet even set up a digital banking unit.
scores.quote: about 95% of the customers into transactions are now going through the digital channel

scores.rationale: Strategy is deliberately matched to customer type — granular retail (62–68% of the book) for stable low-cost relationships with only calibrated, selective large-corporate exposure.
scores.quote: we will continue to pursue a differentiated granular approach to build up more retail business and we will follow a calibrated approach towards the corporate book

scores.rationale: Digital spend is catch-up on commodity rails (UPI, mobile app) with no proprietary technology or R&D intensity, and the DBU build-out has not even begun.
scores.quote: We have not yet set up any DBU to anticipate a person but we do have plans eventually to do that

scores.rationale: Transaction volume runs through UPI, an open public network that commoditises rather than compounds any bank-specific advantage.
scores.quote: UPI has taken the lion's share

scores.rationale: A pan-India branch, ATM and financial-inclusion footprint exists and a supply-chain finance tie-up was added, but nothing in the calls suggests reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: We have done a tie-up arrangement for supply chain finance also

scores.rationale: Capex was starved for years (Rs 8.4bn in Q1FY23, Rs 7.6bn in Q1FY25) and has only recently ramped toward the Rs 500-550bn three-year plan, but incremental returns are poor — Rs 16,000 Crore deployed over six quarters produced only 3% revenue growth and flat cash EBITDA.
scores.quote: we have deployed over Rs. 16,000 Crore and added approximately 30,000 unique broadband towers... The cash EBITDA for FY26 was Rs. 9,217 Crore vs. Rs. 9,198 Crore in FY25

scores.rationale: Heavy award-winning A&P (Cannes Lion, Spikes Asia, CSK/IPL partnership, 'Be Someone's We') has not translated into sales — the subscriber base fell from 240.4mn in Q1FY23 to 192.8mn by Q4FY26.
scores.quote: Vi won the prestigious Cannes Lion award for its human network-testing telecom network campaign

scores.rationale: No meaningful R&D spend disclosed; innovation is sourced from partners (Nokia/Ericsson, Genesys, AWS, C-DOT, PayU, Aditya Birla Capital) with only a recent IoT Innovation Lab as an in-house effort.
scores.quote: Vi Business launched IoT innovation lab India's first telco backed lab for innovation, co-creation & certification of IoT Devices & Application

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed across the 16 calls; the only merger reference is the legacy Vodafone-Idea combination whose integration pain still frames the KPIs.

No dividend or buyback in any call; the entire capital story is repeated massive dilution — Rs 180bn FPO, Rs 20.8bn and Rs 24.6bn preferential issues, OCD conversion, government interest-to-equity conversion of Rs 161.3bn, and now a further Rs 4,730 Crore promoter infusion.
scores.quote: With this equity issuance, VIL has raised INR240 billion of equity, including conversion of OCDs amounting to INR16 billion

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-heavy with no protecting moat — FY26 revenue of Rs 44,873 Crore sits against spectrum/AGR obligations that stood above Rs 2 trillion and a ~527,000-site network requiring Rs 45,000 Crore more capex.
scores.quote: The spectrum obligations to the government stood at INR2,095.2 billion as of June 30, 2024

scores.rationale: Sustained share donation rather than capture — subscribers fell from 240.4mn (Q1FY23) to 192.8mn (Q4FY26), with management celebrating mere stabilisation as a post-merger first.
scores.quote: we have been able to stablise our subscriber base at 192.8 million customers vis-à-vis last quarter, a first since the merger

scores.rationale: No international expansion and domestic footprint has been deliberately narrowed to 17 priority circles, with investment retrenched rather than extended.
scores.quote: We continue to follow focused approach on investing bias towards our 17 priority circles, which contribute over 98% of our revenue

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely pricing- and mix-led — ARPU up for 19 consecutive quarters to Rs 190 on premiumization and a rising 4G/5G mix — while volume (subscribers) has been shrinking throughout.
scores.quote: The Customer ARPU has now been increasing for 19 consecutive quarters... driven primarily by premiumization

scores.rationale: The company is arguably past the trough — AGR dues cut from Rs 87,695 Crore to Rs 64,046 Crore, ICRA upgrade to BBB/Positive, subscribers stabilising and net adds turning positive in Feb-Mar 2026 — but the upturn depends on regulatory relief rather than an industry cycle.
scores.quote: Our AGR dues have been finalised at Rs 64,046 Crore... a reduction from the earlier frozen figure of Rs 87,695 Crore

scores.rationale: The Indian wireless data end market is in secular expansion — data usage per 4G/5G sub up 27.2% YoY to 20.2GB and total traffic up over 30% — though teledensity above 83% limits subscriber-side headroom.
scores.quote: Our data usage in Q4FY26 has also increased YoY by over 30% to 83.0 Petabyte/day

scores.rationale: Leverage is catastrophic and stewardship has been rescue-dependent — gross debt of Rs 1,990.8 billion in FY23, survival contingent on government moratoria, equity conversion, vendor equity swaps and repeated promoter infusions, with investment cut pro-cyclically during the liquidity crunch.
scores.quote: our investments were impacted on account of liquidity constraints over the last few years

scores.rationale: Management has shown tenacity in keeping the business alive across four years, but its long-term plan is not executed independently — capex, 5G timing and even solvency hinge on DoT decisions, lender consortiums and promoter/vendor bailouts.
scores.quote: We remain engaged with lenders to secure the long-term debt financing to support our Capex plans of Rs. 500 billion to Rs. 550 billion

scores.rationale: The executives are low-key career professionals rather than celebrities, but the calls devote substantial airtime to award lists and marketing accolades, and the company sits under constant political and media scrutiny.
scores.quote: At AFAQs Marketers Xcellence Awards 2024, Vi won 5 awards, 2 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze

scores.rationale: Genuine people rhetoric and external validation (Great Place To Work, 15th best company to work for) and two internal CEO successions (Moondra CFO→CEO, Kishore internal→CEO), but the CFO seat was filled externally from Mondelez, indicating an incomplete pipeline.
scores.quote: I'm equally delighted to welcome Mr. Tejas Mehta, as our new CFO, who joins us from Mondel■z

scores.rationale: Communication is unusually transparent about weakness — they publish cash EBITDA alongside reported, strip out IndAS 116 distortions, openly state industry tariffs do not cover cost of capital, and acknowledge subscriber losses rather than spinning them.
scores.quote: further tariff rationalization is needed for the industry to fully cover its cost of capital

scores.rationale: Headline results must be discounted heavily — the FY26 net profit of Rs 34,552 Crore is entirely an accounting write-back from the government's AGR reassessment, not operating skill, since underlying cash EBITDA was flat YoY.
scores.quote: The resulting difference of Rs. 55,622 Crores... has been credited to the P&L as an exceptional item

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere — it is the subscale third private operator, admits a large ARPU discount to peers, and has no captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: I can see we are at a significant discount on an ARPU versus the peers

scores.rationale: Switching costs are near zero under mobile number portability and the company has been the victim of that, shedding 5.2mn subscribers in a single quarter before churn was slowly reduced.
scores.quote: we have been sequentially reducing our churn from 5.2 million to 1.6 million to a 0.5 million last quarter which has increased to a 1 million subscriber loss this quarter

scores.rationale: Indian wireless is a stable three-private-player oligopoly where coordinated tariff hikes of 20-25% flowed straight through to ARPU with minimal consumer pushback, though a state-backed BSNL is now re-emerging.
scores.quote: the industry took of price increase between 20 to 25%... most of it flows straight through in terms of ARPU improvement

scores.rationale: Barriers are formidable — spectrum auctions costing Rs 188bn plus multi-hundred-billion capex deter entrants and pricing has turned rational since 2021 — but management itself concedes returns still fall short of the cost of capital.
scores.quote: The total commitment for the spectrum acquired in this auction is Rs. 188 billion

scores.rationale: Vodafone Idea is itself the share donator in this industry, losing ~48mn subscribers over the period, with analysts probing churn toward a reviving BSNL.
scores.quote: Are you seeing any churn out to BSNL because BSNL reported gross subscriber addition for the month of August to September as per TRAI actually improved

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a systemically important, politically scrutinised, heavily analyst-covered situation whose fate is decided by Supreme Court judgements and DoT committees.
scores.quote: The Hon'ble Supreme Court via its judgement dated October 27, 2025 and November 3, 2025 has permitted the Government of India to reconsider

scores.rationale: Brand affinity is real in awards but does not convert to pricing power — ARPU trails peers materially and growth relies on industry-wide tariff moves plus feature-phone upgrades rather than image-led premium.
scores.quote: we have almost 67% of our customers now on the smartphone and 33% of them being on a feature phone

scores.rationale: Network reliability was once a genuine assurance claim (top TRAI voice quality, fastest 4G in 2022) but years of under-investment eroded it and customers left; only now is coverage being rebuilt to 86% 4G population.
scores.quote: consistent and right investment has been key in stemming our subscriber losses

scores.rationale: Some genuine convenience differentiation — widest international roaming (151 countries, unlimited in 40+), the multi-service Vi app, doorstep SIM delivery and MSME digital tools — but these are add-ons that have not offset core network inconvenience.
scores.quote: Vi remains the only operator in India to provide truly unlimited data and calls in 40+ countries

scores.rationale: The enterprise/corporate franchise is a legitimate relative strength with sticky offerings (SD-WAN, IoT, smart metering targeting 12mn units, CCaaS) leveraging Vodafone Group relationships, while the retail proposition remains weak.
scores.quote: The Smart Metering business aims to deploy 12 million solutions in next three years

scores.rationale: Structurally behind on technology — 5G launched only in March 2025, years after peers, legacy Chinese equipment blocked from 5G upgrades, and no proprietary technology edge.
scores.quote: We have many circles where we have Chinese equipment where 5G is not allowed

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing network effect exists; scale has been shrinking and the digital app ecosystem is entirely assembled from third-party partners rather than owned two-sided platforms.
scores.quote: Our stated strategy around this has been to build this through strategic partnerships

scores.rationale: Distribution/coverage reach is inferior to rivals rather than unmatched — 4G population coverage only crossed 86% in FY26 and 5G reached just 80 cities, well behind competitors' national footprints.
scores.quote: improved our 4G population coverage over 86% on pan India basis

scores.rationale: Heavy and rising growth investment — branches 651 (Jun-22) to 961 (Sep-24), plus a full in-house tech stack — but incremental returns remain thin (ROA ~0.9% ex one-offs, cost-income still 70.7% after seven years), so the spend is growth-oriented yet not yet high-ROIC.
scores.quote: The branch count now stands at 651 branches ... Our branch count is now at 961 branches

scores.rationale: No disclosure of A&P quantum or its return; advertising is mentioned only as a fairness principle, not as brand-building spend.
scores.quote: we hate to put asterisks in our advertisements

scores.rationale: Sustained technology build (the bank's R&D equivalent) has demonstrably produced new products and customers — credit cards from 1mn issued in 2022 to 4.8mn in force by Jun-26, wealth AUM INR64,000 crore — though the payoff on cost is still pending.
scores.quote: customer data platforms, KYC platforms, digital onboarding, payment infrastructure ... the whole stack

scores.rationale: The IDFC Ltd reverse merger was a simplifying, structural deal that added ~24bps to CET-1 rather than a value-adding bolt-on, while the founding Capital First/IDFC Bank merger imported the legacy infra book that has repeatedly hit provisions.
scores.quote: including the benefit which is expected to come in from mergers of about 24 basis points, our CET-1 would be 14.08%

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend policy discussed; the capital story runs the other way — repeated equity issuance, with management conceding book value growth came substantially from raising capital at a premium rather than retained profit.
scores.quote: all of it has not come from raising internal profits, a lot of it has come by raising capital at a premium

scores.rationale: A leveraged, balance-sheet-heavy bank with a 70.7% cost-to-income ratio and ROA only touching ~1% (90bps adjusted) after seven years — the opposite of asset-light with a protecting moat.
scores.quote: if you adjust for it, maybe it will come down to about 90 basis points, not 106 as it is looking

scores.rationale: Small base with a long runway and clear evidence of capture — deposits +32-37%, loans +20-25% versus mid-single/low-double-digit system growth, sustained across all four calls, plus credit cards scaling from 1mn to 4.8mn.
scores.quote: Y-o-Y growth in deposits is now 32% for the Bank ... Retail deposits was up 37%

scores.rationale: Credible, well-executed domestic footprint expansion (651→961 branches) plus an NRI deposit franchise of INR25,000 crore, but this is national branch build-out, not a premium brand travelling into new markets.
scores.quote: now we're talking about INR25,000 crores of NRI deposits in the bank

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led: NIM has compressed from 6.18% (Q2FY25) to 5.96%, savings rates were cut to 3%, and mix has shifted toward lower-yield secured/mortgage/corporate lending.
scores.quote: the net interest margin on an AUM improved by 3 basis points to 5.96%

scores.rationale: The bank is emerging from the bottom of the microfinance credit cycle that crushed FY25-26 earnings, with slippages down 30% YoY, MFI SMA normalised to 0.71% and PAT up 132% YoY — an identifiable upturn now underway.
scores.quote: in microfinance, I would say things have largely got restored on the asset quality front

scores.rationale: Indian retail credit and deposit penetration is in secular expansion, evidenced by four years of uninterrupted 20%+ book growth across mortgages, vehicle, cards and wealth even through a credit shock.
scores.quote: customer business ... has crossed INR6 lakh crores during the quarter and we saw a Y-o-Y increase of almost about 20%

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, deliberate exit from infrastructure lending, repayment of high-cost legacy borrowings and voluntary counter-cyclical provisioning of INR515 crore show prudence, though repeated dilutive capital raising tempers the score.
scores.quote: we have created a contingency provision of INR515 crores. This is purely I would say voluntary and on a prudent basis

scores.rationale: A seven-year build executed against sustained scepticism, methodically resolving INR14,000 crore of legacy stressed loans one by one through courts and ARCs while rebuilding the deposit franchise.
scores.quote: We have Rs. 14,000 crores of such loans which we identified, and we have dealt with it, dealt with it over the last 5 years

scores.rationale: The CEO is a high-profile, narrative-forward communicator who repeatedly makes bold forward claims and references his own conference-circuit presence — the opposite of low-profile.
scores.quote: you have to look nearly 2 years forward, and let me tell you, you'll probably surprise yourself

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly credits employees and stresses hiring quality technology people, but no systematic talent-development programme or internal succession pipeline is described across the four calls.
scores.quote: having the right quality of people, and building a stack inside out

scores.rationale: Consistently owns misses in plain language — apologises for the toll-road surprise, admits the cost-income target was got wrong, and voluntarily strips out treasury and tax one-offs to show a lower true ROA.
scores.quote: In fact, in the first round I got it wrong because we thought we'll fix it in five years; it's been seven years, we're still dealing with it

scores.rationale: Separating results from skill is unflattering: the 2022 promise of 45% compounding core profit and never posting a loss again gave way to FY25 provisions collapsing PAT to INR201 crore, and much of the book-value gain came from equity issuance rather than earned returns.
scores.quote: It is frankly our read that our bank will never post a loss again in its life

scores.rationale: Retail banking products here — mortgages, vehicle loans, cards, deposits — are commoditised with no aftermarket or mind-share monopoly; the bank competes as a challenger on service, not position.
scores.quote: Housing finance is stable and growing, so I think it's growing for everybody

scores.rationale: There is genuine deposit stickiness — retail deposits still grew 37% after the savings rate was cut to 3% — but no regional monopoly or contractual switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: this is despite the fact that we dropped savings account rates to 3% last to last quarter

scores.rationale: Indian banking is a fragmented field of large private, PSU, small-finance banks and NBFCs where depositors and borrowers shop freely on rate; the bank must pay 5.96% cost of funds to hold its book.
scores.quote: reduction in cost of fund, which further came down from 6% to 5.96%

scores.rationale: RBI licensing is a hard entry barrier and ownership is stable post-merger, but pricing is anything but rational — deposit rate competition and the sector-wide microfinance overlending episode both show discipline breaking down.
scores.quote: microfinance is an issue and we cannot wish it away because the microfinance portfolio is disturbing in many parts of India

scores.rationale: Weak-franchise PSU banks, stressed NBFCs and retreating MFI lenders are ceding retail and corporate share, letting the bank grow deposits and loans at roughly twice system rates and now push corporate lending at 30%.
scores.quote: in wholesale, we continue to power up and there the growth was even stronger at 30%

scores.rationale: A listed, heavily covered bank with brokerage-hosted quarterly calls, rating-agency scrutiny and constant media attention on its legacy exposures — nothing under the radar.
scores.quote: which eventually did not default, but gave us all quite a scare and fright and bad news in the media

scores.rationale: The customer-first, no-asterisks, no-hidden-fees positioning builds goodwill but management explicitly declines to monetise it, and NIM is drifting down rather than showing pricing power.
scores.quote: We don't charge fees just because the customer doesn't notice, just because you don't notice I can't bill you

scores.rationale: Depositors are buying safety over rate — CRISIL upgraded the FD programme to AAA and retail deposits compounded 37% even after the savings rate was cut, showing trust dominating price.
scores.quote: on the fixed deposit program, CRISIL has rated us AAA, which to us is a huge arrival moment

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine strength — 961 branches, a well-regarded app, digital onboarding and call-centre stack, with fee income up 22.9% on 25%+ disbursement growth indicating an effective distribution engine.
scores.quote: All of you are experiencing what a fantastic technology stack that you have ... how our app is being experienced by our customers

scores.rationale: The benefit type matches the customer: an overwhelmingly retail franchise (92% of fees from retail, retail/agri/MSME INR2.4 lakh crore) served with intangible trust-and-fairness positioning rather than corporate TCO arguments.
scores.quote: Now 92% of the fee is contributed by the retail book

scores.rationale: A deep, self-built multi-layer stack spanning onboarding, decisioning, data streaming and AI is a real capability supporting cross-sell, but it is asserted rather than evidenced as superior to larger private-bank peers.
scores.quote: risk and decisioning engines, API, data streaming, machine learning, artificial intelligence, the whole stack

scores.rationale: Nothing in the model is self-reinforcing across two sides — deposits and loans are each won customer-by-customer through rate, branch reach and marketing, with the bank paying up in cost-to-income to acquire each one.
scores.quote: cost to income ratio excluding trading gains improved by 166 basis points on a sequential basis to 70.7%

scores.rationale: 961 branches plus a strong digital channel give respectable reach, but it is a fraction of large private-bank networks and branch additions have slowed sharply (only 17 opened in a half-year), so rivals can match it.
scores.quote: During this half year, we have opened about 17 branches for the year

scores.rationale: As an asset-light exchange, growth 'capex' takes the form of platform/technology build-out and greenfield subsidiaries (IGX, ICX, Indian Coal Exchange) funded internally at very high incremental returns, though absolute capex is small and never quantified.
scores.quote: with the approval of the (IEX) Board have already incorporated Indian Coal Exchange Ltd – a separate company for this purpose

scores.rationale: Across all four calls management never discusses advertising or promotional spend as a brand-building lever; the only promotion references are rivals' fee incentives, which IEX explicitly declines to match.

Consistent product/technology development over the period — web bidding, APIs, EnergyX, green DAM/RTM, peak contracts, 15-minute to 5-minute granularity — has repeatedly yielded new tradable segments, though several new products remain stuck awaiting CERC approval rather than converting to revenue.
scores.quote: Technology is our strong area. And in the last two three years we have introduced many products in the market

scores.rationale: There are no acquisitions in the five-year record — every expansion (IGX 2020, ICX, Indian Coal Exchange, proposed mineral exchange) is greenfield incorporation, so the parameter has no bolt-on track record to reward or penalise.
scores.quote: IEX also incorporated Indian Gas Exchange in 2020

scores.rationale: A coherent, regular distribution policy is evident — a final dividend of INR 2 per share (200% of face value) out of INR 492.9 crore FY26 PAT, plus monetising the IGX stake via IPO — but no valuation-sensitive buyback is described in these excerpts.
scores.quote: The Board of Directors have announced a final dividend of INR 2 per share, equivalent to 200% of face value

scores.rationale: The business is extremely asset-light with ~66% net margins (FY26 revenue INR 747 crore, PAT INR 492 crore) on a liquidity-network moat, but that moat is being directly attacked by CERC's market coupling regulation, which caps the score.
scores.quote: consolidated revenue growth of 13.6% at Rs.747 crore. And our PAT was Rs. 492 crore

scores.rationale: IEX is already dominant at 80-85% share with essentially no runway to gain, and the realistic direction of travel is share loss once market coupling is implemented.
scores.quote: Leading energy exchange for all these years, we have always been maintaining 80 -85% market share

scores.rationale: The business is entirely India-domestic and the one cross-border attempt (carbon exchange for European buyers) was abandoned over currency/GST issues and shelved pending GIFT City approvals.
scores.quote: we found that India is a net seller of carbon credits and buyers are there in the European market

scores.rationale: Growth is almost purely volume-led with adverse price realisation — FY26 volumes rose 17% while consolidated revenue rose only 13.6% — because the transaction fee is regulated (CERC has repeatedly forced fee justification) and mix is shifting to lower-yield segments.
scores.quote: electricity volumes touched 141 billion units, higher by 17% on a year-on-year basis

scores.rationale: FY26 was a cyclical trough — flat national consumption on a good monsoon and mild summer — with a visible upturn already underway in FY27 (12% peak demand growth, El Nino ahead), positioning the company near the bottom of the demand cycle.
scores.quote: peak demand was almost about 271 gigawatt in the month of May... with about 12% increase in peak demand

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion: renewables past 50% of installed capacity four years early, demand projected toward 2,700 BU by FY32, and exchange-traded share of consumption rising from ~4-5% to 8% as BESS, VPPA, CfD and un-requisitioned surplus rules push volume onto exchanges.
scores.quote: power demand is expected to approach almost about 2,700 billion units with a peak demand of 388 gigawatt by FY’32

scores.rationale: Management has grown entirely organically with no leverage and no acquisitions, funding new exchanges from internal accruals and monetising IGX via IPO, though the widening spread into gas, carbon, coal and now minerals carries some scope-creep risk.
scores.quote: we have already filed a DRHP (Draft Red Herring Prospectus) for IPO of IGX as we today hold 47.3% in IGX

scores.rationale: Goel has led continuously since FY2021 with multi-year persistence on the same agenda — chasing the 11-month TAM contract and green RTM approvals for over two years and appealing market coupling to APTEL — but execution depends on a regulator that keeps orders reserved, limiting true independence.
scores.quote: we continue to await approval from the CERC on a petition to extend the Term Ahead Market contract to 11 months

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently substance-heavy on policy, volumes and product mechanics with no personality-building; the same low-profile team fronts every call and defers to colleagues for detail.
scores.quote: Today, I along with the Management Team of IEX will brief you about our business performance, our strategy and future outlook

scores.rationale: Clear internal promotion pipeline across the period — Rohit Bajaj moved from Head of Business Development (2022) to Executive Director (2024) to Joint MD (2026), with Amit Kumar and Aparna Garg similarly elevated — indicating systematic internal development.
scores.quote: represented by Rohit Bajaj, JMD, Vineet Harlalka, Company Secretary and CFO and Amit Kumar, Executive Director

scores.rationale: Management quantifies bad news rather than hiding it — putting a specific 20-40% DAM impact on market coupling, disclosing why the carbon exchange was shelved, and flagging subdued FY26 demand — although the 2024 claim that IGX would match IEX's size has visibly not tracked (IGX PAT INR 42 crore vs IEX INR 492 crore).
scores.quote: even if there is an impact, it may be about 20, 30, 40% (in DAM)

scores.rationale: The exceptional financials are substantially a product of a first-mover regulated position and government liquidity mandates (LPSC rules, Section 11 directives) rather than demonstrable operating skill, and the same regulator is now able to dismantle the advantage — so results should not be read as management quality.
scores.quote: these policy initiative s can make a lot of difference. This has already brought in a lot of liquidity on to the exchange platform

scores.rationale: IEX holds a monopoly-like position in the customer's mind with 85% share and effectively universal participant registration — every DISCOM, merchant RE generator and conventional IPP trades on it — making it the default venue for Indian power.
scores.quote: all distribution utilities are with us, all renewable merchant generators are trading with us, all conventional IPPs are also registered with us

scores.rationale: Deliberate switching costs have been engineered through API integration into customers' bidding and back-office systems plus data analytics, which management itself calls a 'tight coupling' intended to survive regulatory market coupling.
scores.quote: We have done API integration with our customers for the purpose of bidding and also for the purpose of back office

scores.rationale: The structure is a dominant player with two fringe rivals (PXIL, HPX) rather than a stable oligopoly, and while end customers have no individual pricing power, the regulator negotiates on their behalf through fee scrutiny and coupling.
scores.quote: HPX has started operation from 6th of July with only one segment which is Day Ahead Contingency (DAC) market

scores.rationale: Barriers proved permeable — HPX entered in 2022, rivals used promotional fee incentives to buy TAM/REC volume, and the regulator has capped fees and is now mandating market coupling with Grid India as operator, which removes the structural barrier entirely.
scores.quote: CERC issued an order on implementing market coupling on 23rd July 2025... the regulator decided to initiate the process of implementation

scores.rationale: Weak competitors do exist but at 85% share there is very little left to take, and the flow of share is more likely to reverse under coupling than to continue toward IEX.
scores.quote: in the first quarter our market share has been almost about 85% and in the month of July, we are maintaining a market share of almost about 89%

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a high-profile listed near-monopoly whose fees have been repeatedly challenged by CERC and whose core market is being restructured by regulation, drawing both new entrants and intense analyst and policy attention.
scores.quote: CERC had asked you to justify on the transaction fees

scores.rationale: Gross margins are exceptional and management cites 18 years of accumulated trust, but pricing power is not image-driven and is explicitly constrained — the transaction fee is regulator-set and has had to be justified to CERC.
scores.quote: with the kind of trust which we have built over the years in these last 18 years

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty — transparent price discovery, guaranteed and timely settlement, and payment discipline enforced through exchange access — with the tiny transaction fee clearly secondary to that reliability.
scores.quote: exchanges have helped in disciplining the sector and the results are there to see

scores.rationale: Accessibility and customer intimacy are the explicitly stated differentiator across the whole period — web-based bidding, API automation, online reconciliation, data analytics and continuous direct engagement — and management is betting market-share retention on it post-coupling.
scores.quote: we launched the web-based bidding platform to provide our customers anytime, anywhere, easy, and secure access to the trading system

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/institutional (DISCOMs, gencos, IPPs, C&I) and IEX matches it correctly with TCO benefits — replacing costlier power at INR 3.86/unit — plus integration-based lock-in rather than brand appeal.
scores.quote: 9,000 plus participants, all distribution utilities are with us

scores.rationale: A genuine multi-product platform edge exists — 15-minute trading ahead of Europe, readiness for 5-minute RTM, API and analytics layers — but R&D intensity is modest and the technology is not the binding constraint on rivals, since regulation is.
scores.quote: Earlier it used to be one hour trading. We (IEX) started with 15 minutes. In fact, in Europe very recently they moved to 15-minute trading

scores.rationale: A textbook two-sided liquidity network — near-universal buyer and seller registration draws further liquidity, which is why 85% share persisted despite two rival exchanges — yet market coupling is designed specifically to socialise that liquidity across exchanges, capping the durability.
scores.quote: Huge participant base, 9,000 plus participants, all distribution utilities are with us

scores.rationale: Reach across every category of market participant plus dedicated customer engagement and integration teams gives a service footprint rivals have not matched in 18 years, though this is registration reach rather than a physical distribution asset.
scores.quote: We keep interacting with the customers, understand their problem and try to provide solutions to them

scores.rationale: Capex is modest and largely capacity/platform catch-up (~INR500cr over 6 years, INR89cr in FY26 of which only INR43cr in appliances) with company PBT margin still ~3%, so incremental ROIC on growth spend is poor.
scores.quote: Current year total company-wide number is INR 89 crores... home appliance division is around INR 43 crores

scores.rationale: Promised ATL brand spend repeatedly failed to materialise while trade discounts/schemes rose to 26% of gross sales — spend is buying volume, not brand equity.
scores.quote: we had also mentioned that we will see something on the A&P front, at least on the ATL side. But I think those 2 things have not actually materialized

scores.rationale: Product development consistently lags the market — IFB missed the entire 12kg front-load segment that grew to ~13% of the market and is only now launching 13/14kg, with 'filling product gaps' a running theme for three years.
scores.quote: we currently don't operate in the 12 kg... we'll be launching a 13 kg and a 14 kg in the front loader in this year

scores.rationale: The M&A pipeline described was neither small nor strictly complementary — 7-8 targets of INR300cr+ including 'niche' areas outside their competence — and no completed, margin-accretive bolt-on is evidenced.
scores.quote: We have about 7, 8 companies that we are looking into... the sizes are a minimum of INR300 crores, going upwards... areas which are niche, etcetera, which we are not in

scores.rationale: No discussion of buybacks, dividends or any distribution policy anywhere in the excerpts.
Turnover is reasonable (INR5,476cr revenue on light annual capex) but there is no protecting moat — 26% of gross sales given away in schemes and an inability to pass through costs leave PBT at ~3%.
scores.quote: our channel schemes and discounts, they have gone up by 100 basis points. So from 25% of gross sales, it has gone to 26-odd percent

scores.rationale: Genuine runway and some capture: top loader share rose to ~9-10% with ~19% volume growth, and AC share is only ~3-3.5%, though front-load share has been flat-to-slightly-up at ~23%.
scores.quote: Top loader, we are currently 9%... full year, we have grown by about 19 percentage in top loader

scores.rationale: Beyond a passing 2022 note that BLDC motors would target overseas customers, geographic expansion is not discussed or quantified in any call.
scores.quote: we are targeting both domestic as well as overseas customers

scores.rationale: Recent SKU rationalisation and premiumisation are pushing revenue growth above volume growth (front load +11% revenue vs +7% volume), but the company repeatedly cannot pass on forex/commodity costs, showing weak pricing power.
scores.quote: our revenue growth is significantly higher than our volume growth in most of the segments... ideally, we would have liked to pass on everything to the customer. But today, that's not possible

scores.rationale: Cyclicality shows up as weather/commodity volatility (early monsoon killing the AC season, copper above 12,000 LME) rather than a positioning near an identifiable cycle bottom.
scores.quote: ACs, growth was muted... because of the early monsoons, etcetera, also the AC industry showed a major dip

scores.rationale: The Indian appliance market shows secular expansion and premiumisation — a 12kg+ segment appearing from nothing to ~13% of the market on dual-income/larger-capacity demand.
scores.quote: 12 kg actually is a new emerging segment... today, it contributes to almost 13 percentage of the overall market

scores.rationale: Focus is organic and management showed prudence in fixing creditor payments and ROCE and in doing consultant-scoped work in-house, but the same decision cost them the FY24 AC season and a INR300cr+ M&A hunt was simultaneously open.
scores.quote: we also wanted to streamline creditor repayments... we ran short. And we also ran short in April, May

scores.rationale: The double-digit-margin promise has been rolled forward from FY23 ('fully fixed in Q4 of this year') through FY24 ('Q2 and Q3 of this year') to FY26, where PBT is still ~3.3%, so tenacity on cost programmes has not converted into the stated long-term outcome.
scores.quote: we would expect in Q2 and Q3 of this year, to be able to get to those levels

scores.rationale: Consistently low-key, functional calls run by CFOs and divisional heads with no promotional or celebrity posture, and disclosure kept deliberately minimal.
scores.quote: No, sorry, sir. We don't give gross margin indication.

scores.rationale: Persistent churn at the top — three MDs exited over FY21-FY24 and the Home Appliances MD role was filled externally in April 2026 — points to a weak internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: Mr. Sandeep Joseph Abraham, MD and CEO of our Home Appliance division, who has recently joined on 8th of April

scores.rationale: Management openly owns misses and quantifies headwinds — admitting they failed to foresee AC demand, that washer sales are inexplicably weak, and that large OEMs left for better options — even while withholding gross margins and unit volumes.
scores.quote: we just did not foresee it... the washer sale has not moved up to the extent that we want. And we are putting a lot more emphasis on that

scores.rationale: Little halo risk since results are visibly mediocre, but recent profit protection is attributed to a cost-innovation programme offsetting forex/commodity rather than to demonstrated durable skill.
scores.quote: the impact on commodity as well as forex was INR 32 crores and INR 52 crores totaling to INR 84 crores. But INR 67 crores of that, we were able to make up because of our cost optimization program

scores.rationale: IFB holds a respectable mind-space in front-load washers (~23-26% addressable, No. 2) but explicitly not a monopoly-like position, and is marginal in AC at ~3%.
scores.quote: We are currently number two in this. But there are people different categories. There are one or perhaps two or three who are major players

scores.rationale: No switching costs are evident — OEM customers simply walked away to cheaper suppliers and consumers are won with cashbacks and free kits.
scores.quote: a couple of OEMs... who used to pick large volumes from us have stopped, and presuming that they're getting better options from somewhere else

scores.rationale: The category is crowded and the end customer/channel holds the power, with multinationals pricing aggressively and dealers extracting schemes.
scores.quote: a player like Samsung has been extremely aggressive in terms of pricing in the market over the last two quarters

scores.rationale: Low barriers and irrational pricing: competitors absorbed 13-16% material inflation while raising prices only 4-6%, new entrants reached ~10% washing-machine share faster than IFB, and IFB's own discounts keep climbing.
scores.quote: the material cost increase was anywhere between 13% and 16%... but if you look at the two main players their price change in the market was between 4% and 6%

scores.rationale: IFB is more often the donator than the taker — flat front-load share, 3% in AC and OEM volumes lost — with competitors described as stronger, not weaker.
scores.quote: when you look at some of the other players who had entered the market much later than us, they have reached about 10% market share in washing machines

scores.rationale: Consumer durables in India is a capital-magnet category contested by global majors, not an ignored niche — competitive intensity is a standing agenda item on every call.
scores.quote: when we go to channels and see, we just see too many players

scores.rationale: Pricing power from image is weak — costs cannot be passed through, discounts are rising, and margins depend on internal cost programmes rather than brand-led realisation.
scores.quote: we are looking at opportunities to increase our prices wherever it is possible... that's not possible because of competitive and our relative position in the market

scores.rationale: There are hints of a reliability/service proposition (a service-cost line, premiumisation, front-load leadership), but no evidence customers accept a price premium for trust.
scores.quote: we are able to push this entire thing of premiumization

scores.rationale: Distribution intimacy is a genuine, persistently worked asset — a multi-year channel-extraction agenda, counter sales representatives, broadened counter presence and a rising e-commerce mix.
scores.quote: we are also working on improving our productivity through our counter sales representatives

scores.rationale: The retail side lacks intangible pull (bought with cashbacks and free kits) while the corporate/OEM side shows zero lock-in as large accounts defected on price.
scores.quote: we had given higher promotion scheme per customer like cash back, free IFB essential kits

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology edge — 20-30% of COGS is imported including compressors, electronics localisation is framed as a cost exercise, and product features follow the market rather than lead it.
scores.quote: Product to product, it differs. It is between 20% to 30%

scores.rationale: A single-sided product-sales model with dealer schemes and OEM contracts; nothing in the business strengthens with scale in a self-reinforcing way, and OEM churn confirms the absence.
scores.quote: some of the big OEMs, which used to pick up big volumes from us earlier are more or less stopped

scores.rationale: A real owned service and counter-level sales network exists, but reach is admittedly sub-scale versus rivals — low wallet share at key counters and only ~3% AC share show rivals can and do match it.
scores.quote: our wallet share in some of the counters have been quite less

scores.rationale: Capex is explicitly growth-linked (new labs, capacity ramp, Italy operations, extra office space) and sits alongside exceptional incremental returns of 48% group ROCE / 70% India ROCE, though the absolute quantum is small in this asset-light model.
scores.quote: The DNA setup , step up is reflective of the incremental capex consistent with volume and business scale-up

scores.rationale: A&P stepped up materially and deliberately from near-zero (ICC Women's World Cup, IPL/Gujarat Titans, 'Heera Ki Asli Pehchan') and management accepted margin drag for it, but the brand-equity payoff is still unproven.
scores.quote: the quarter saw the impact of discretionary brand and marketing spends resultant of the IPL sponsorship, which is largely front-loaded

scores.rationale: No R&D line or new-product pipeline is discussed; the only technology investment cited is AI/ML applied to internal turnaround times and efficiency rather than product creation.
scores.quote: integrating AI and ML into our operations to further enhance service qualities, improve customer turnaround times, increase operational efficiencies

scores.rationale: The AGL deal is a textbook small, complementary bolt-on of an already-strong niche leader that is immediately accretive (+3% revenue, +2% EBITDA), though the earlier Rs 1,345 crore Belgium/Netherlands purchase was a large IPO-funded related-entity consolidation.
scores.quote: The AGL acquisition led to an incremental 3% revenue growth, with the base business delivering 20% revenue growth for this quarter

scores.rationale: No buyback, dividend or capital-return policy is mentioned anywhere across the excerpts.
A debt-free, asset-light certification model throws off 48% consolidated and ~70% India ROCE with 60%+ EBITDA margins, protected by a trust-based certification moat.
scores.quote: the group has delivered extremely strong returns on capital employed, which stands at 48%, and a return on equity at 47%

scores.rationale: Already dominant in India (>50%) and LGD (65% global) which limits runway there, but there is a clear, actively pursued share-gain runway in global natural-diamond loose stones and coloured stones.
scores.quote: We are working to gain market share in natural diamond loose stones, winning new customers and growing our share of wallet with existing ones

scores.rationale: Expansion is real and ongoing — 10 countries/31 labs, Italy commenced via Belgium, AGL to be taken global, strong Middle East and China — but the US and European entities have been soft for several quarters.
scores.quote: We also commenced operations in Italy through our Belgium subsidiary as we continue to explore geographical expansion

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led with pricing flat by management's own repeated admission, and realisation has at times fallen on mix (-5% consol in Q3 CY25), with recent ASP gains coming from AGL consolidation rather than price.
scores.quote: we are seeing stability in pricing, there has not been any significant change in this quarter

scores.rationale: The end market faces headwinds (gold/silver price spikes, tariffs, ND jewelry down 19% then +2%) but management identifies no cycle bottom or upturn, treating the driver as structural instead.
scores.quote: ND Jewelery saw a 19% decline due to a slowdown in the India ND jewelry business caused by steep increase in prices of gold and silver

scores.rationale: Certification intensity is structurally rising as LGD expands the affordable-diamond consumer base, with India penetration still early — the clearest secular tailwind in the business.
scores.quote: the diamond industry today is witnessing a structural increase in certification intensity across all categories

scores.rationale: The company is debt-free, funds growth internally, invests through industry headwinds and keeps M&A small post-IPO, though the Rs 1,345 crore subsidiary buy-in was a large, if pre-committed, transaction.
scores.quote: The company continues to be debt-free.

scores.rationale: Strategic priorities have been held constant and delivered on for multiple years, and management explicitly subordinates near-term margin to long-haul investment.
scores.quote: those two strategic priorities which have been on record for the last two years continues to be our core focus areas

scores.rationale: The MD and CFO communicate in a plain, results-focused register with no personality-building, even while the company itself runs high-visibility consumer campaigns.
scores.quote: We remain committed to enabling growth for our partners, delivering long-term value to all our stakeholders.

scores.rationale: There is systematic gemologist training via 18 in-house schools, but the senior bench is being built by external recruitment (COO from Reliance Brands, new US leadership) rather than an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: Mr. Manu Sharma joining us as the Chief Operating Officer, who brings over 20 years of leadership experience in retail luxury

scores.rationale: Management voluntarily strips out the inorganic AGL contribution and explains margin dips and the intercompany commission mechanics, but repeatedly declines to give segment revenue splits.
scores.quote: In line with maintaining transparency, there is two months of revenue for this period which is now got consolidated

scores.rationale: Superb reported metrics are hard to separate from an extraordinary structural LGD tailwind and an inherited near-monopoly position, so skill cannot be cleanly isolated from circumstance.
scores.quote: we are at an inflection point as far as lab grown diamond goes

scores.rationale: IGI occupies a definitional position in the customer's mind for lab-grown certification, holding ~65% global LGD share, where its certificate is what confers the product's identity.
scores.quote: IGI certificate for lab-grown diamonds makes a lab-grown diamond a diamond. Otherwise, without certification, it can be considered just as a piece of glass.

scores.rationale: In-factory and mobile labs physically embedded at manufacturers, plus nine of India's top ten chains as customers, create real switching friction, though customers can and do use rival labs.
scores.quote: We have 31 laboratories, 12 in-factory lab setups, 18 gemological schools, and we serve over 7,500 customers globally

scores.rationale: Certification at scale is a very tight field of a few players with fragmented, low-power customers across the value chain, though it is closer to a duopoly than a broad oligopoly.
scores.quote: The gems and jewelry certification market has a very high entry barrier, with only a select few operating at a scale.

scores.rationale: High stated entry barriers plus repeatedly confirmed pricing stability over many quarters despite an industry downturn indicate no discount war and no meaningful new entrants.
scores.quote: We have seen a lot of stability in pricing over the last three, four quarters.

scores.rationale: Clear share is available in global natural-diamond certification where IGI is under-indexed and is actively winning accounts, aided by new LGD customers migrating up to natural.
scores.quote: the consumption of natural diamonds certified by IGI is also on the uptick

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a Blackstone-backed recent IPO with IPL and World Cup sponsorships and heavy sell-side coverage, in a sector attracting abundant capital.
scores.quote: backed by the able guidance of Blackstone, the world's largest alternate investment manager

scores.rationale: The product is essentially a trusted mark whose perceived authority commands 60%+ consolidated and ~70% India EBITDA margins with demand holding through industry headwinds.
scores.quote: EBITDA margins at 60.9%, representing a 230 bps year-on-year improvement

scores.rationale: The entire value proposition is certainty and trust — buyers purchase assurance of origin and the 4Cs, with price explicitly secondary to confidence.
scores.quote: we are in the business of giving consumer confidence and trust to buy a diamond

scores.rationale: Multiple delivery formats put the lab inside the customer's factory or at their doorstep, backed by overseas marketing offices that source retailer leads and are paid commission for them.
scores.quote: IGI laboratories, in-factory laboratories, mobile labs, strengthening our customer relationships and driving a distinct advantage

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — reliability and embedded workflow lock-in for B2B manufacturers and chains, with new consumer campaigns building the retail intangible.
